report.summary:
Verdict: the sandwich works inside the existing FrontRooms/Surface shader, it is cheap, and URP's lighting model already behaves the way the user wants. With _Metallic = 0, URP builds the specular colour as lerp(0.04, albedo, metallic), so it stays 0.04 whatever the albedo is. An albedo-only print layer therefore only changes the diffuse term. Highlights, the normal, smoothness and cavity all come from the static paper layer (the "skin"), provided those inputs never contain the pattern. (Verified in URP 17.3 BRDF.hlsl:93.)

Real wallpaper is built in the same order as the sandwich: substrate, then ground coat, then printed ink films, then a clear vinyl/acrylic coat, then embossing done after printing (sources below).

The blocker is the current texture set. The chevron ink is baked into the normal map (0.9*blur(ink)), smoothness (+0.07*ink) and cavity (-0.10*ink). I measured the generator's height terms. Once filtered to mip 1 or higher, which is every view beyond about 0.5 m at FOV 76 and 1080p, the chevron term is 94-98% of the slope energy left in the normal map. The 1.17 mm weave term disappears entirely. So today's lit relief at play distance is essentially the chevron. If only the albedo animates, the old chevron stays visible in the shading as a "ghost". gen_surfaces.py wallpaper() must be split into paper-only albedo/normal/mask, a separate print-coverage texture with one channel per ink plate, and an optional separate ghost-emboss map.

The DepthNormals pass (URP DepthNormalsPass.hlsl) writes only the interpolated mesh normal: no _BumpMap and no PlanarFrame. SSAO is therefore computed from flat walls and can never see the print or the emboss. That is desirable here.

Recommendation: option (a). Extend FrontRoomsSurface.shader with a shader_feature_local_fragment _FR_PRINT path, plus an optional _FR_PRINT_GHOST.
- Inks are composited in linear space onto the paper, in press order: a ground flood, then plates 1-4. Each plate has a transparent/opaque mix and Murray-Davies coverage, with an optional Yule-Nielsen n. n of about 2.2 reproduces today's sRGB-space duotone.
- Static ageing (foxing, seam shadow, blots, macro wear, grime) is applied afterwards as multiplicative filters, so ink never covers a stain.
- New material properties go into the shared UnityPerMaterial CBUFFER unconditionally, which keeps the shader SRP Batcher compatible.
- The motion coverage arrives as a global texture or render texture (RT). Per-wall variation can use Renderer Shader User Value (available in 6.3) rather than MaterialPropertyBlocks, which break SRP batching.

Rejected options:
- (c) Complex Lit clear coat: a single shared normal, about twice the lighting cost, not needed.
- (d) URP decals: no DBuffer on WebGL/GL ES, the receiving shader needs DBuffer keywords anyway, decals don't use the SRP Batcher, and the screen-space variant lights the decal with the flat reconstructed normal.
- (e) Detail maps: a static x2 multiply on mesh UVs.
- (b) Shader Graph: only as a prototyping or Custom Render Texture authoring tool for the motion layer. Its generated DepthNormals pass uses mesh tangents, which conflicts with the world-planar frame.

All rendering files are owned by the visual chat. This is a spec; no files were edited.

findings.topic: Physical wallpaper construction (layer order)
findings.claim: Wallpaper is physically a stack: backing/substrate, ground coat, printed ink, then often a coating that seals the ink, with embossing after printing. This is the same order as the user's sandwich.
findings.detail: [Verified] Encyclopedia.com (How Products Are Made) says wallpaper 'consists of a backing, ground coat, applied ink'. Pulp sheets are coated with kaolin, TiO2 for opacity and latex, or with coloured PVC, before printing. Wallpaperinstaller.com (installer trade reference) says vinyl-coated papers have the decorative surface 'sprayed or coated with an acrylic coating', and some papers have coatings 'to seal in the inks'. In-register embossers accept preprinted rolls, i.e. the emboss is applied after printing (embossing-roller patent; NS Packaging trade report on a machine that 'accept[s] preprinted rolls ... in-register'). [Inference] PBR mapping: substrate and ground coat give paper albedo and texture modulation (skin). Ink gives albedo only (print). Clear topcoat gives the specular lobe and smoothness (skin). Emboss gives the normal (skin), and is pattern-registered only if the manufacturer chose that. Ageing and soiling sit on top of everything.

findings.topic: Printing methods and ink behaviour
findings.claim: Ink behaviour depends on the process. Surface printing deposits heavy ink that 'creeps'. Gravure uses transparent inks, with depth of tone set by cell depth. Rotary screen gives opaque, crisp colours dried between stations. Flexo uses less ink and is more exact. Machine printing leaves 'merely a film of colour' on the sheet.
findings.detail: [Verified] Wallpaperinstaller.com printing-methods page: surface printing lays down 'very heavy amounts of ink'. Rotogravure inks are transparent and 'the deeper the color desired, the deeper the recessed pocket'. Rotary screen gives 'vibrant opaque colors, with crisp edges', with colours dried between stations. Flexo 'allows the use of less ink and provides a more exact image'. Wallpaper History Society: roller printing uses one roller per colour, each fed by its own tray; relief rollers used water-based colours and intaglio rollers oil-based ones. V&A (Morris & Co. Bower, 1877 cover sheet): 'MACHINE-PRINTED PAPERS ... merely a film of colour deposited on the surface'. [Inference] Each ink plate needs an opacity parameter: 0 means a transparent filter (gravure/flexo process ink), 1 means opaque body colour (screen/surface). Because machine-printed ink is a thin film, even opaque ink should keep the paper's fibre/mottle modulation, which is why the shader passes a mean-1 'paperTex' into the opaque branch.

findings.topic: Embossing: mechanical vs chemical, registered vs unregistered
findings.claim: Chemical embossing couples the relief to the print: an inhibitor ink stops the foam from rising, so recesses fall exactly under the printed areas, beneath a clear wear layer. Mechanical in-register embossing aligns a heated roller to a preprinted roll. An unregistered (texture) emboss is independent of the print.
findings.detail: [Verified] US5824721: inhibitor ink printed on a foamable plastisol; 'expansion in the printed areas containing the inhibitor is retarded, resulting in a textured surface with depressions in those areas printed with the inhibited ink'. Samples were then 'coated with 10 mils of a clear plastisol wearlayer'. This patent is mainly about floor and wall coverings. Mechanical embossing passes heated material between an embossing roller and a backing roller (patent 20100326295). Cooper Hewitt holds period examples such as the embossed-vinyl sidewall 'Signet', ca. 1990, Scot Simon. That metadata comes from the search index; the object page returned HTTP 500 when fetched. Anaglypta (1887 onward) is an embossed relief paper designed to be painted after hanging (Designing Buildings wiki; V&A O77065). It is a historical case of a static relief skin with colour applied separately. [Inference] The user's rule (lighting from the skin only) physically matches a flat-printed vinyl-coated paper with an unregistered texture emboss, or an Anaglypta-style relief painted later. It does not match chemical or registered embossing, because there the relief follows the print.

findings.topic: Ink compositing models
findings.claim: Area coverage composites linearly in reflectance (Murray-Davies), with an empirical Yule-Nielsen n for optical dot gain. Reflected light passes through a transparent ink twice. Continuous coverage in the shader is the correct pixel-scale average of a halftone.
findings.detail: [Verified] Murray-Davies: R = (1-a)R0 + a*Ri. Yule-Nielsen inserts a power 1/n to account for lateral light scattering in paper (optical dot gain; Wikipedia 'Dot gain'; IS&T literature in search results). Reflected light 'transmits the ink layer twice' (EPFL transparent-ink model, search summary). [Inference] One texel is 0.366 mm (0.75 m / 2048), so gravure cells and screen meshes are sub-texel. Render coverage as continuous and do not draw dots. Composite in linear space; Unity already linearises sRGB textures in this Linear-colour-space project (ProjectSettings m_ActiveColorSpace: 1). Mixing in R^(1/n) space with n of about 2.2 is mathematically almost the same as today's gen_surfaces.py duotone, which is interpolated in sRGB-encoded values. So _DotGainN ≈ 2.2 reproduces the current look, and n = 1 gives pure Murray-Davies. A side effect: with n > 1, a motion-graphics cross-fade between two prints darkens in the middle like overprinted ink, rather than dissolving like a screen. Misregistration means each plate samples coverage with its own small offset (fractions of a mm to 1-2 mm). Registration is a known critical issue in roller and surface printing, and that error stays in albedo only.

findings.topic: URP specular is independent of albedo at metallic 0
findings.claim: Under URP's metallic workflow with _Metallic = 0, the specular colour is constant (F0 = 0.04) and albedo only scales the diffuse term. An albedo-only print therefore cannot change highlights or reflections. No second BRDF layer is needed for the topcoat.
findings.detail: [Verified, local source] BRDF.hlsl:93 has brdfSpecular = lerp(kDielectricSpec.rgb, albedo, metallic), with kDielectricSpec = 0.04 (BRDF.hlsl:9), and brdfDiffuse = albedo * oneMinusReflectivity. The wallpaper SurfaceDefs leave metallic at 0. [Inference] The user's 'texture layer above the motion graphic' is already the single specular lobe of UniversalFragmentPBR, as long as s.smoothness, s.normalTS and s.occlusion come only from the skin. Any ink-dependent smoothness term, such as today's +0.07*ink, makes the sheen move with the animation, so it should default to 0.

findings.topic: Current textures entangle ink with lighting inputs (measured)
findings.claim: At gameplay distance, the chevron-registered height term is 94-98% of the visible normal-map relief. Smoothness (+0.07*ink on a 0.20 base, a 35% relative gain) and cavity (-0.10*ink) are also chevron-registered.
findings.detail: [Verified, local source] gen_surfaces.py:68 has height = .18*weave + .9*blur(ink,1.2) + .40*fib + .6*seam. Line 70 has smooth = .20 + .07*blur(ink) ... and line 71 has cav = 1 - .35*seam - .10*ink. [Measured] I reproduced the terms with the CC0 source in a scratchpad script, writing nothing to the project. At full resolution, the shares of gradient energy are weave 76%, ink 11%, fibre 12%, seam 1%. After blurring at sigma 2, 4 and 8 texels (roughly mip 1-3), ink is 94.1%, 96.5% and 98.0%, while weave is 0%. Ink edges tilt the normal up to about 12 degrees at bump 0.8, against about 3.6 degrees for the fibre p99. Pixel footprint at FOV 76 and 1080p is about 1.45 mm/px at 1 m, i.e. about 4 texels (mip ~2). [Inference] If only the albedo animates, the old chevron stays as the dominant shading pattern. A paper-only normal map will also look much flatter than today at distance, because the weave period is 3.2 px (1.17 mm) and filters out. A lower-frequency, unregistered skin emboss (a period-typical stipple or linen vinyl texture at about 2-6 mm) is needed to keep the paper reading as paper.

findings.topic: DepthNormals pass vs forward normal (SSAO)
findings.claim: The shader's DepthNormals pass writes the interpolated mesh normal only. It uses neither _BumpMap nor PlanarFrame, so SSAO sees flat walls while the forward pass shades with the world-planar TBN times the normal map.
findings.detail: [Verified, local source] The shader includes Packages/.../Shaders/DepthNormalsPass.hlsl. Its DepthNormalsFragment outputs NormalizeNormalPerPixel(input.normalWS), where input.normalWS comes from GetVertexNormalInputs, and it samples _BaseMap only under _ALPHATEST_ON, which is not defined here. URP Lit's own LitDepthNormalsPass samples the normal map under _NORMALMAP, so this custom shader departs from Lit's convention. SSAO is configured with Source = 1 (depth normals) and Radius 0.45 m in FrontRoomsRenderSetup.EnsureSsao. [Inference] The geometric normal is identical in both passes, so there is no macro mismatch. For the sandwich this is ideal: SSAO cannot react to the print or to any ghost emboss, and the 0.45 m radius could not resolve a 1-2 mm emboss anyway. No change to the DepthNormals pass is needed. Note that material occlusion (cavity) only feeds indirect light: CreateAmbientOcclusionFactor takes min(ssaoIndirect, occlusion), per AmbientOcclusion.hlsl:59.

findings.topic: SRP Batcher compatibility
findings.claim: The shader is SRP Batcher compatible today: one UnityPerMaterial CBUFFER declared in HLSLINCLUDE and shared by all four passes. New print properties must be added to that same block unconditionally. The motion texture can be a global, and per-renderer data must avoid MaterialPropertyBlocks.
findings.detail: [Verified] Unity 6.3 docs: material properties must sit in a single UnityPerMaterial constant buffer, and a GameObject 'mustn't use MaterialPropertyBlocks'. The SRP Batcher works on draws 'that use the same shader variant'. Unity forum (staff): the UnityPerMaterial layout must be identical across all variants of a subshader, so it must not be wrapped in #ifdef. Shader.SetGlobalTexture: globals are used only when the material does not define the property, e.g. when it is not in the Properties block. Renderer Shader User Value exists in 6.3 (MeshRenderer.SetShaderUserValue, read as unity_RendererUserValue). Unity docs say it 'doesn't interfere with batching' and is faster than MaterialPropertyBlocks. URP 17.3 UnityInput.hlsl:177 defines it from unity_RenderingLayer.y inside UnityPerDraw. [Inference] Add _FR_PRINT as shader_feature_local_fragment. The wallpaper materials then form their own variant batch, which they effectively do already. Never put _FR_PrintCoverage in Properties.

findings.topic: Option (c) Complex Lit clear coat
findings.claim: Rejected. URP clear coat uses the same normal as the base, roughly doubles lighting cost, lives in Complex Lit (heavier, Shader Model 4.5), and is not needed because the single dielectric lobe already acts as the topcoat.
findings.detail: [Verified] The Unity 6.1 Complex Lit docs say clear coat 'has roughly twice the cost of rendering a base material, because the lighting is evaluated once per layer', with coat IOR 1.5. The choose-a-shader page calls Complex Lit 'considerably more resource-intensive' and says it requires Shader Model 4.5. Locally, Lighting.hlsl:65 evaluates the coat with DirectBRDFSpecular(brdfDataClearCoat, normalWS, ...), the same normalWS as the base. ComplexLit uses UniversalForwardOnly. [Inference] The custom shader could enable _CLEARCOAT and set s.clearCoatMask, because UniversalFragmentPBR supports it. But there are many realtime lights per pixel in Forward+, the coat cannot have its own smooth normal over a rough paper, and satin vinyl (smoothness about 0.2) does not need a second lobe. Not worth it.

findings.topic: Option (d) URP Decal Projector / DBuffer
findings.claim: Rejected for the whole wallpaper; fine for a local event such as a single changing patch. DBuffer is not supported on OpenGL/GL ES (so not WebGL2), needs a depth-normals prepass, needs the receiving shader to opt in, and decals don't use the SRP Batcher. Screen-space decals are lit with depth-reconstructed (flat) normals.
findings.detail: [Verified] Unity decal reference: DBuffer 'Albedo' affects 'base color and the emission color'. DBuffer does not support OpenGL/OpenGL ES and requires a depth-normal prepass. Screen-space decals render after opaques 'using normals that Unity reconstructs from the depth texture'. Decals 'do not support the SRP Batcher by design because they use Material property blocks'. Decals do not work on transparent surfaces. Locally, URP Lit applies DBuffer only via #pragma multi_compile_fragment _ _DBUFFER_MRT1 _DBUFFER_MRT2 _DBUFFER_MRT3 and ApplyDecalToSurfaceData (Lit.shader:148, LitForwardPass.hlsl:255). FrontRooms/Surface has neither, so decals would currently not affect it at all. ApplyDecal composites baseColor*w + rgb, an 'over' blend. [Inference] Called at the end of Frag the way Lit does it, a decal print would cover the stains, which is the wrong order. A custom shader could call ApplyDecalToBaseColor before the wear section to fix that, but it still costs projector draws per room, extra full-screen DBuffer render targets and no WebGL, and gives nothing that sampling the print directly in world-planar UV does not.

findings.topic: Option (e) detail maps and option (b) Shader Graph
findings.claim: Detail maps are a static multiply on mesh UVs and cannot do opaque inks or palettes. Shader Graph would mean rebuilding PlanarFrame and macro wear, and its generated DepthNormals pass uses mesh tangents for tangent-space normals. Use Shader Graph only to author the motion layer (Custom Render Texture target), not the wall shader.
findings.detail: [Verified] URP LitInput.hlsl:224-227 computes detailAlbedo = 2.0*detailAlbedo and returns albedo * LerpWhiteTo(detail, mask), a multiply-overlay on a static texture with a second UV set. The Lit docs describe Detail Inputs as overlays. Shader Graph's URP DepthNormalsOnlyPass.hlsl:46-47 builds the tangent-space normal from unpacked.tangentWS (the mesh tangent). The Lit graph can output a world-space normal instead via Fragment Normal Space = World. Shader Graph supports a Custom Render Texture target. [Inference] Porting the 90-material uber-shader to Shader Graph adds variants and risk for no gain. The x2 'detail' convention is still a useful precedent for the mean-1 paper modulation. A Shader Graph Custom Render Texture or full-screen graph is a good designer-friendly way to author the coverage plates that feed the hand-written surface shader.

findings.topic: Correct layer order
findings.claim: Order: world frame, then SKIN (paper substrate and ground-coated sheet: albedo modulation, normal, cavity), then PRINT (ground flood, then plates 1..n in press order, albedo only, with per-plate misregistration), then ABOVE-PRINT ageing (foxing, seam shadow, blots/tide marks, topcoat yellowing via _BaseColor), then the existing macro wear (tone, dirt, stains, floor grime, ceiling streaks), then UniversalFragmentPBR with skin normal, smoothness and occlusion, then fog.
findings.detail: [Inference, grounded in the sources above] Order only matters for non-multiplicative operations. Every existing macro-wear line in Frag multiplies albedo (or edits smoothness/normal), so it can stay exactly where it is after the print. The one place order bites is an opaque ink 'over': if stains were baked into the paper before printing, an opaque plate would hide them and the stains would appear to slide behind the animation. Two of today's albedo terms are not multiplicative and must change. The brown blot over-composite (col*(1-tob)+brown*tob) becomes a transparent brown multiply above the print, which is physically right for a deposited stain. The seam 'lift' (+0.04 additive) should be dropped from albedo, since it is lighting and the seam height term is already in the normal. The only allowed wear-to-print interaction is wear reducing ink coverage (bleaching or fading of fugitive inks). The print must never modify wear.

findings.topic: Ghost of the old pattern (static registered emboss under a changing print)
findings.claim: Keeping the chevron emboss in the skin while the print changes produces a shading-only chevron: in register when the print is the chevron, misregistered when the print scrolls, and a colourless relief when the print shows something else. Make it a separate optional map with its own strength, not a leftover.
findings.detail: [Inference, using the measurement above] Where it shows: (1) the top band of each wall under the troffers, where ceiling light rakes the wall at grazing incidence and the relief has the most contrast; (2) specular sheen at grazing view angles down long corridors, if the +0.07 old-ink gloss is kept; (3) in rooms where fixtures are dead and only the trilight ambient remains, through cavity, which in URP affects indirect light only; (4) it changes contrast as fixtures flicker independently, because the relief responds to the light direction. It is physically plausible as a misregistered or unregistered emboss on a re-run print (registration problems are real; batch/run shade variation between rolls is documented by Graham & Brown). It reads diegetically as 'the wall remembers the chevron'. Suggested use: _GhostEmboss 0 in Lobby and Exit, about 0.5-0.8 in Shift.

findings.topic: Coordinate and rebase constraints for the motion layer
findings.claim: Sample the print in the same PlanarFrame 'metres' as the paper, so it never swims. Its horizontal period must divide 192 m. Any procedural motion that uses world position must be 192 m-periodic, or use un-rebased coordinates.
findings.detail: [Verified, local source] FrontRoomsRoomStream.RebaseIfNeeded shifts Z by floor(z/192)*192 (RebaseThreshold = 192f, described as a 'multiple of every world-projected period'). Walls use world Y for V, which is never rebased. The current wallpaper tile is 0.75 m x 1.125 m: 192/0.75 = 256, while 1.125 does not divide 192, which is fine because it is vertical. [Inference] Print repeats of 0.75, 1.5, 3, 6, 12 or 24 m horizontally are safe. The RoomStream already tracks TotalRebaseShift, which the motion system could publish as a global so motion phases do not jump. The coverage render texture needs mipmaps, trilinear filtering, anisotropic filtering and repeat wrap, or the chevron will shimmer at grazing angles. The importer gives static textures this already: mips, trilinear, aniso 16.

findings.topic: Stale docs and texture-pipeline notes
findings.claim: Several docs still describe the old 256/373 m roll and 256 m rebase. The importer already treats any non-_A/_E/_N texture as linear, so new _Print_P and _Ghost_G maps import correctly without importer changes.
findings.detail: [Verified, local source] The gen_common.py docstring, the gen_surfaces.py header, and VISUAL_RESEARCH_LOOKDEV.md line 106 say 'wallpaper 256/373 m ... divide 256'. FrontRoomsRenderSetup and LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC give Roll = 0.75 m and a 192 m rebase. FrontRoomsSurfaceTextureImporter sets sRGB only for stems ending in _A or _E and NormalMap for _N; everything else is linear with CompressedHQ and mips. BACKROOMS_WALLPAPER_RESEARCH.md (stale) once stated 'The pattern is albedo-only', which is the same principle the sandwich returns to.

recommendations: Implement option (a) in FrontRoomsSurface.shader, owned by the visual chat. Add `#pragma shader_feature_local_fragment _ _FR_PRINT` and `#pragma shader_feature_local_fragment _ _FR_PRINT_GHOST` to the ForwardLit pass only. Leave ShadowCaster, DepthOnly and DepthNormals unchanged; the print never touches depth or normals. If a material's keyword will be toggled at runtime rather than set on the asset, use multi_compile_local so the variant is not stripped from builds.

Append the new properties (_PaperMean, _InkGround, _Ink1-4, _PrintTile, _Misreg12/34, _PrintStrength, _DotGainN, _InkGloss, _GhostEmboss, _PaperStainColor) to the existing HLSLINCLUDE UnityPerMaterial block with no #if around them, so the layout is identical in every pass and variant. Declare _FR_PrintCoverage outside the CBUFFER and outside Properties so it works as a global.

Feed the motion layer through a global coverage texture (RGBA = 4 ink plates, linear, mipmapped, repeat wrap). A small [ExecuteAlways] controller should set it to the static chevron program by default, so edit mode and missing-controller cases still show the classic paper. Swap in a render texture (RT) for animation. This avoids Material.SetTexture on shared Resources materials, which would rewrite the assets during editor play mode. Add per-wall program or phase later via MeshRenderer.SetShaderUserValue, never via MaterialPropertyBlocks.

Split gen_surfaces.py wallpaper() into five outputs (see code spec): <name>_Paper_A (sRGB, paper only, mean-1 modulation in linear), <name>_Paper_N (weave + fibre + seam, no ink), <name>_Paper_S (R smoothness, G cavity, B above-print ageing multiplier, A blot alpha), <name>_Print_P (linear RGBA plates: mid = saturate(2t), deep = saturate(2t-1), accent, cream), and an optional <name>_Ghost_G (RG chevron-emboss normal XY, B old-ink density). Keep the current maps as the non-keyword fallback until the switch is approved.

Collapse Wallpaper_Chevron and Wallpaper_Chevron_Cold into one skin plus one print program plus two palettes, set through SurfaceDef fields (Lobby/Shift: ground #D2C27C, mid #AC9A52, deep #766A34, cream #E3D594; Exit: #AFC0B6 / #87998F / #56655E / #C5D3C9). Treat these as 'the same paper under a different print run', which is what the code comment already says. This removes the duplicate A/N/S texture set.

Start with _DotGainN = 2.2 and all plates opaque (alpha 1) to match today's look, then validate side by side in the Frame Debugger and in-game. Keep _InkGloss = 0, because any ink-driven gloss makes the sheen follow the animation and breaks the user's rule.

Do not keep the chevron emboss implicitly. Default _GhostEmboss = 0. Add an unregistered, period-plausible texture emboss (stipple or linen at roughly 2-6 mm) to the paper normal, so the skin still reads as paper at mip 1-3 once the chevron relief is removed. Expose the ghost as a deliberate per-room-profile dial (for example Shift 0.5-0.8).

Optional realism that stays albedo-only: per-roll misregistration and shade jitter, hashed from floor(metres.x / 0.75), on the order of 0.5 mm and about 1-2% shade, matching run/batch variation. Also per-plate misregistration offsets (_Misreg12/34), which can be animated as plates drifting.
Keep motion phases continuous across the 192 m Z rebase: use print periods that divide 192 m horizontally, or publish RoomStream.TotalRebaseShift as a global offset for procedural motion.
Use Shader Graph only to author the coverage plates (Custom Render Texture target or a full-screen graph writing the RT). Do not port FrontRooms/Surface to Shader Graph.

Update the stale docs (gen_common.py docstring, gen_surfaces.py header, VISUAL_RESEARCH_LOOKDEV.md §Surfaces) to 0.75 m / 192 m when the split lands, and add the print-texture contract to LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC under the visual chat.
open_questions: Which visual chat owns the change, and when: FrontRoomsSurface.shader, FrontRoomsRenderSetup.cs SurfaceDef fields and gen_surfaces.py all belong to it. Should Exit keep its own palette or become a different print program?

What does the motion layer actually do: slow pattern drift or scroll, plate misregistration, cross-fades between motifs, or reactive events? This sets the plate count (4 RGBA channels vs a Texture2DArray of programs) and the RT resolution and update rate.
Should the ghost emboss be a narrative device (Shift rooms only), or should the walls be pattern-free in relief everywhere?
For WebGL2 as a secondary target: confirm unity_RendererUserValue and RT mip auto-generation behave there. DBuffer decals are documented as unsupported on OpenGL/GL ES, so they are already out.

Confirm in the Frame Debugger that the colour properties used as ink palettes arrive linearised in this Linear-space project. Generator hex values are sRGB; the existing _StainColor relies on the same behaviour, but this was not re-verified on the 6.3 docs.
Which unset-global default does Unity bind for a missing _FR_PrintCoverage in edit mode? Not verified. The recommendation is to always set it from a controller to avoid finding out.
Is the 1.17 mm weave term in the current normal map intentional? It vanishes by mip 1, so it only matters within about 0.5 m of the wall.

code.title: FrontRoomsSurface.shader: HLSLINCLUDE additions (append inside the existing UnityPerMaterial block; never inside #if)
FrontRoomsSurface.shader ForwardLit: PrintPlate() helper + composite that replaces the three texture samples at lines 185-187 of Frag()
gen_surfaces.py wallpaper(): split spec (illustrative, not applied; reuses today's seeds and helpers)
code.code:
def wallpaper_split(name="Wallpaper_Chevron", paper_hex="#E6DFC9"):
    # --- unchanged source analysis (lines 37-44) ---
    # src, big, lum, ink (= t), cr (cream mask), chroma = big - lum[..., None]
    # fib, mot, blot, fox, dd, seam_shadow, weave exactly as today (same seeds)

    # 1) PRINT program -> <name>_Print_P.png  (linear RGBA; importer keeps non-_A names linear)
    plate_mid  = np.clip(2 * ink, 0, 1)            # ground -> mid
    plate_deep = np.clip(2 * ink - 1, 0, 1)        # mid -> deep
    plate_acc  = accent_mask(chroma)               # optional: pink/slate band of the CC0 scan, else zeros
    plate_crm  = cr * .55                          # cream ink at today's 55 % strength
    save_rgba(f"{OUT}/{name}_Print_P.png", np.stack([plate_mid, plate_deep, plate_acc, plate_crm], -1))
    # palette -> SurfaceDef: _InkGround=ground(a=1) _Ink1=mid(a=1) _Ink2=deep(a=1) _Ink3=accent _Ink4=cream(a=1)

    # 2) SKIN albedo -> <name>_Paper_A.png (sRGB). Modulation built in LINEAR, mean 1.
    mod = srgb_to_lin((0.97 + 0.06 * mot) * (0.988 + 0.024 * fib))
    mod /= mod.mean()
    paper_lin = srgb_to_lin(hexc(paper_hex))
    save_rgb(f"{OUT}/{name}_Paper_A.png", lin_to_srgb(paper_lin * mod[..., None]))
    # -> SurfaceDef._PaperMean = paper_lin   (no duotone, no hue, no cream, no blots/fox/seam here)

    # 3) SKIN normal -> <name>_Paper_N.png : NO ink term.
    height = .18 * weave + .40 * fib + .6 * np.exp(-((dd - 2) / 2.2) ** 2)
    # + recommended: an UNREGISTERED period texture emboss at ~2-6 mm so relief survives mip 1-3
    save_normal(f"{OUT}/{name}_Paper_N.png", normal_from_height(height, 1.0))

    # 4) SKIN mask + ABOVE-print ageing -> <name>_Paper_S.png (linear RGBA)
    smooth = .20 + .07 * ink.mean() - .04 * mot + .03 * (1 - fib)  # same mean gloss, no pattern
    cav    = 1 - .35 * seam_shadow / .20                            # seam only (ink term removed)
    ageing = (1 - .09 * fox) * (1 - seam_shadow)                    # multiplicative, above print
    blot_a = np.clip((blot - .64) / .25, 0, 1)                      # full-range alpha
    save_rgba(f"{OUT}/{name}_Paper_S.png", np.stack([smooth, cav, ageing, blot_a], -1))
    # -> SurfaceDef._PaperStainColor = 1 - .08 * (1 - lin(#7A5B2A) / lin(ground))  (today's 8 % blot)
    # seam_lift (+.04 additive) is dropped: it is lighting, already in the normal's seam term.

    # 5) optional GHOST -> <name>_Ghost_G.png (linear RGBA): the chevron emboss on its own
    g = normal_from_height(.9 * blur(ink, 1.2), 1.0)
    save_rgba(f"{OUT}/{name}_Ghost_G.png",
              np.stack([g[..., 0] * .5 + .5, g[..., 1] * .5 + .5, blur(ink, 1.0), np.ones_like(ink)], -1))

verdicts.claim: Physical construction: vinyl-coated papers are sprayed or coated with acrylic, some papers are coated to seal in the inks, gravure inks are transparent with depth set by cell depth, rotary screen gives opaque crisp colours dried between stations, and machine printing leaves 'merely a film of colour' (V&A O251080). Chemical embossing via inhibitor ink gives depressions under the printed areas beneath a 10-mil clear wear layer (US5824721).
