The V&A API record O251080 (Bower, 1877) contains 'there is merely a film of colour deposited on the surface of the paper'. US5824721 contains the inhibitor/depression sentence and 'coated with 10 mils of a clear plastisol wearlayer', in the context of floor and wall coverings. The encyclopedia.com, Cooper Hewitt and NS Packaging citations were not checked.

verdicts.claim: RoomStream rebases Z by floor(z/192)*192 and tracks TotalRebaseShift. Walls use world Y for V (never rebased). Roll = 0.75 m divides 192. The importer makes only _A/_E stems sRGB and _N normal maps, and everything else is linear CompressedHQ with mips, trilinear and aniso 16. Several docs still say 256/373 m.
verdicts.evidence: FrontRoomsRoomStream.cs:52 RebaseThreshold = 192f; lines 943-964 shift Z only and accumulate TotalRebaseShift (public getter at line 237). PlanarFrame (FrontRoomsSurface.shader ~line 157): for wall normals t = cross(up, n) and b = cross(n, t) = world +Y. Roll = .75f (FrontRoomsRenderSetup.cs:32). FrontRoomsSurfaceTextureImporter (FrontRoomsRenderSetup.cs:617-641) matches the claim, but applies only under /Resources/Surfaces/Textures/. gen_common.py docstring, gen_surfaces.py header and VISUAL_RESEARCH_LOOKDEV.md:104-106 still say 256 and 256/373. BACKROOMS_WALLPAPER_RESEARCH.md:24 says 'The pattern is albedo-only'.

verdicts.claim: Every existing macro-wear term in Frag multiplies albedo (or edits smoothness/normal), so it can stay after the print unchanged. The generator's blot over-composite and +0.04 seam_lift are the non-multiplicative terms.
verdicts.evidence: Frag (FrontRoomsSurface.shader:189-221): tone*dirt multiply; the stain lerp(albedo, albedo*_StainColor*1.6, w) equals albedo*lerp(1, _StainColor*1.6, w), which is multiplicative though it can brighten above 1x; wet multiplies and edits smoothness/nTS; floor grime multiplies; the ceiling streak lerp is multiplicative. gen_surfaces.py has `col = col*(1-tob) + hexc('#7A5B2A')*tob` and `+ seam_lift`. The shader never reads mask.b or mask.a; generator B is an unused 'wet' slot, since wet comes from the macro map. So repurposing B and A for ageing and blot alpha is safe.

verdicts.claim: Mixing in R^(1/n) with n ≈ 2.2 reproduces today's duotone, because gen_surfaces interpolates in sRGB-encoded values; all-opaque plates mid = saturate(2t), deep = saturate(2t-1) reproduce ground→mid→deep.
verdicts.evidence: hexc() returns raw sRGB-encoded 0-1 values with no linearisation, and the duotone lerps those. Sequential opaque lerps with c1 = sat(2t) and c2 = sat(2t-1) exactly reproduce the piecewise duotone. But sRGB is not a pure 2.2 power, and the mottle/fibre multiply is applied in encoded space today, i.e. about mod^2.2 in linear. The report's paperTex is normalised in linear space, and the keep_hue chroma residual is only reproduced if an 'accent' plate is built. Cream at 55% strength composites on top in encoded space. The match is approximate, not exact.
verdicts.correction: Expect a close but not identical match. The keep_hue chroma term (0.16 Lobby, 0.10 Exit) is lost unless a fifth plate or palette term carries it, and the paper modulation contrast will differ slightly. Validate side by side.

gaps: Global-texture limitation: one global _FR_PrintCoverage is shared by every FrontRooms/Surface material with _FR_PRINT (Lobby, Shift, Exit). Different print programs per material or per room need a per-material texture (which then is in Properties and shadows the global), a Texture2DArray indexed by a material float or by RSUV, or separate globals. The report mentions RSUV for 'phase' but does not resolve how Exit vs Lobby pick different programs.

RSUV values are not serialized and reset on reload (6000.3 SetShaderUserValue docs). RoomStream pools and reuses room roots, so the value must be re-applied every time a room is (re)built. The report does not mention this.

Shader keyword handling: the report proposes shader_feature_local_fragment for _FR_PRINT. FrontRoomsRenderSetup regenerates materials (Set up URP menu) and has a 'keep metallic/emission' re-apply path around lines 528-537. Any new keyword or properties must survive that regeneration path, or the materials lose the print setup. Not addressed.

Performance on the stated secondary target (WebGL2): the print path adds 4 extra taps on an RGBA RT (one per plate for misregistration), all trilinear plus aniso, on every wall pixel, in a scene with many soft-shadowed point/spot lights. On WebGL the RT, its auto-mip generation (RenderTexture.useMipMap/autoGenerateMips) and Custom Render Texture support should be checked. The report lists the mip question as open but does not estimate cost; collapsing to 1-2 taps with fixed misregistration is an obvious fallback.

RT mip quality: an animated coverage RT regenerated with box-filtered auto mips at runtime will alias differently from the offline 2048x3072 import (CompressedHQ/BC7). Fast motion in world-planar space can shimmer at grazing angles even with aniso. RT resolution and update rate relative to the 0.75 m tile are not specified.

The measurement uses Gaussian blur on height as a proxy for mips of a compressed normal map. Real normal-map mip averaging shortens vectors and Unity renormalises, which further flattens. So 'paper looks flatter at distance' is if anything understated. The 'ink tilts normal ~12 degrees' figure was not reproduced.

Code issue: the ground flood uses PrintPlate(..., _PrintStrength) and then cov is also multiplied by _PrintStrength. So _PrintStrength scales the plates twice relative to the ground (quadratically), which may not be intended.

Code issue: _Ghost_G stores emboss normal XY in a default-type linear texture that is BC7-compressed by the importer. The decode path is fine, but compression of a packed normal in a non-normal-map texture may band. Using a _N-suffixed ghost (imported as NormalMap) would be safer.

Unverified citations: encyclopedia.com, Cooper Hewitt object (the report itself notes HTTP 500), NS Packaging, the justia embossing patent, the Unity forum thread on the CBUFFER layout across variants, the EPFL and IS&T ink-model papers, and the Graham & Brown batch-number page were not fetched in this verification.
Behaviour of an unset global texture in edit mode (which default Unity binds) is still unverified. The report correctly flags it and mitigates with an [ExecuteAlways] controller.

Physical-plausibility nuance: the report rightly notes chemical and registered emboss couple relief to print, which contradicts the user's rule. The 1990 vinyl-coated wallcoverings typical of the era were often textured or embossed vinyl. So an unregistered texture emboss (as recommended) is the period-plausible choice, but this should be backed by a 1990 trade source before treating it as era-locked fact.

report.summary:
I compared six ways to produce the animated print (the motion-graphic layer of the user's wallpaper "sandwich") against FrontRooms' actual code and settings. I made no file changes, downloaded nothing and did not launch Unity.

**Recommended primary approach: a hybrid of (b) and (a).**
- **(b) The frames:** an authored Texture2DArray of ink keyframes. Each frame stores a signed distance field (SDF) in R and anti-aliased coverage in G, at 512x768 per 0.75 x 1.125 m tile. The student designs the frames in Figma or After Effects and a script packs them.
- **(a) The motion and filtering:** done in the existing FrontRooms/Surface wall pass.
  - Pick the frame from a global clock, with an optional per-roll phase offset and a world-space "wave" offset.
  - Blend the two neighbouring frames' SDFs, which reads as a shape morph, not a ghosting crossfade.
  - Anti-alias the ink edge analytically with fwidth up close, and switch to the mipmapped coverage channel at distance so grazing walls don't shimmer.
- **Binding:** the array is bound once with Shader.SetGlobalTexture. It is declared outside UnityPerMaterial and outside the Properties block, which is how URP 17.3's own Lit reads globals (_ScreenSpaceOcclusionTexture, _GlossyEnvironmentColor). So the SRP Batcher is not affected.
- **Lighting:** ink only multiplies albedo. Normal, smoothness and cavity come only from the paper layer, so light and reflections follow the paper, not the print.
- **Why this one:** it runs the same on Metal and WebGL2 (texture arrays are supported on WebGL 2.0) and adds no render passes. Every wall is driven by one clock, so all walls stay in sync and survive the 192 m Z rebase. It is also the only family besides pure procedural that allows per-roll phase offsets.

**Fallbacks:**
- **Live 2D stage (A):** for freeform motion that can't be reduced to keyframes. Render a UI Toolkit panel (PanelSettings.targetTexture) to a texture, using Figma SVGs through Unity 6.3's built-in SVG importer, which the project already uses for its logo. The Rive runtime (renders to a RenderTexture on Metal and WebGL) is an alternative. This gives one shared texture with mips, but per-roll phase offsets are lost.
- **Pure procedural (B):** a math-only chevron in the shader. Zero memory, but the student can't author shapes in Figma or After Effects.

**Not recommended as the main system:**
- **(c) VideoPlayer:** the Video module isn't in the manifest. On WebGL, video only plays from a URL, with no frame accuracy. A Unity A/V developer says seamless looping is not achievable on most platforms.
- **(d) CustomRenderTexture reaction-diffusion:** keep it for one-off "mutation" events. It isn't reproducible and doesn't look like 1990 printing.
- **(f) Compute:** WebGL2 has none, and WebGPU is experimental in 6000.3.

**Project issues found:**
- The ink is currently baked into the wallpaper's albedo, normal, smoothness and cavity maps. The generator has to be split into an ink-free paper set plus a print set.
- The texture importer for Resources/Surfaces/Textures forces a 4096 px size cap and CompressedHQ, which would shrink a flipbook sheet and waste memory on a one-channel mask. The print needs its own import rule.
- WebGL's default quality level sets anisotropic filtering per texture, so the print texture must set anisoLevel explicitly.
- Desyncing individual rolls conflicts with the "every 3 m wall module looks the same" rule (TileAlign). Hashing per roll within each 3 m cell keeps the rule; hashing across 256 rolls (192 m) breaks it, and that needs the owners' decision.

All of these files belong to the visual chat.

findings.topic: Project fact: how wall UVs and periods constrain any print
findings.claim: The print must tile in 'tile space' = world metres / (0.75, 1.125). Horizontal periods must divide 3 m (TileAlign = Cell) and therefore 192 m. The vertical period is free because the rebase only shifts Z.
findings.detail:
FrontRoomsSurface.shader PlanarFrame (lines 157-162):
- U = dot(posWS, t), with t = normalize(cross(up, n)), so U runs along world X or Z. V = world Y.
- uv = metres / _TileSize (line 183). Wallpaper tile = (Roll, Roll*1.5) = 0.75 x 1.125 m (FrontRoomsRenderSetup.cs lines 32, 272-278).
- 0.75 m = 4 rolls per 3 m cell, 32 per 24 m chunk, 256 per 192 m WorldPeriod.

The rebase: FrontRoomsRoomStream.cs lines 943-944 shift the world in Z by multiples of 192 m. LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC §5 says vertical repeats are 'Free' (the paper is cut at the ceiling). So 1.125 m not dividing 192 is fine.

TileAlign: FrontRoomsModuleUnits.cs line 20 says 'World-projected tile sizes must divide this so every 3 m wall module looks the same'. So legal horizontal print periods are 0.75, 1.5 and 3.0 m.

Inference: any shader hash keyed on roll index must be periodic in 256 rolls (strip & 255) to survive a rebase, or in 4 rolls (strip & 3) to keep the module rule.

findings.topic: Project fact: the ink is baked into the lighting maps today
findings.claim: wallpaper() bakes the ink into the normal, smoothness and cavity maps as well as albedo. For the sandwich (lighting from the texture layer only), the generator must emit an ink-free paper set plus a separate print/SDF source.
findings.detail:
In Tools/lookdev/gen_surfaces.py, wallpaper() bakes ink into:
- height: 0.9*blur(ink,1.2) (line 68), which feeds the normal map
- smoothness: +0.07*blur(ink) (line 70)
- cavity: -0.10*ink (line 71)
- albedo: the duotone (line 47)

Belongs to the paper layer: the roll-seam shadow/lift (lines 60-64), fibre, mottling, blots and foxing.

Inference:
- The existing `ink` array is the ideal frame 0 of the print. Threshold it at 0.5 and run a distance transform to get frame 0, so today's static look is preserved exactly when the clock is stopped.
- The paper albedo should be the 'ground' colour. The ink becomes a multiplicative tint (deep/ground ratio) applied in the shader before macro wear, so stains and grime sit on top and never animate.

findings.topic: Project fact: installed modules decide which pipelines are free
findings.claim: The Video module is not in the project, so VideoPlayer would need com.unity.modules.video added. UI Toolkit (com.unity.modules.uielements, pulled in by inputsystem) and Unity 6.3's built-in SVG to VectorImage importer are already used.
findings.detail:
Packages/manifest.json lists only ugui, inputsystem, audio, physics, jsonserialize, ui, imageconversion, screencapture and URP 17.3.0. packages-lock.json resolves com.unity.modules.uielements.

FrontRooms3DGame.cs uses UIDocument, PanelSettings and VectorImage, loading Resources/Brand/*.svg. The .svg.meta files use the built-in ScriptedImporter (guid 0000...e000).

Unity's Vector Graphics 3.0 docs say Unity 6.3 'includes a built-in Vector Graphics module with native support for importing SVG files', and the package is needed only for Sprite/uGUI import types. The Video module page names it com.unity.modules.video.

findings.topic: Project fact: import rules and anisotropic filtering settings that would bite the print
findings.claim: FrontRoomsSurfaceTextureImporter forces maxTextureSize 4096 and CompressedHQ on everything under /Resources/Surfaces/Textures/. Standalone defaults to Ultra (aniso ForceEnable) but WebGL defaults to High (aniso per-texture), so a runtime RT or array must set anisoLevel itself.
findings.detail:
FrontRoomsRenderSetup.cs lines 617-640: mipmaps, Trilinear, anisoLevel 16, Repeat, maxTextureSize = 4096, CompressedHQ. sRGB is on only for names ending _A or _E. textureShape is not touched, so a manual 2D Array shape would persist.
- Consequence: a flipbook sheet in that folder is capped at 4096 px before slicing. 8x4 frames of 512x768 = 4096x3072 fits; 1024x1536 frames fit only 4x2 = 8 frames.
- CompressedHQ on a mask picks an RGBA format (inference), wasting memory. Give the print its own folder and rule: linear, R8G8/BC5 or R8/BC4, mips, aniso 16, Repeat.

QualitySettings.asset: Standalone default = 5 (Ultra, anisotropicTextures 2 = ForceEnable); WebGL default = 3 (High, anisotropicTextures 1 = Enable 'as set for each texture').

Texture.anisoLevel doc: range 0-16. Under Forced On, anisoLevel 0 disables aniso for that texture and 1-9 clamp to 9. With Metal/Vulkan/OpenGL, aniso and mip filtering are controlled independently.

findings.topic: One shared global print texture without breaking the SRP Batcher
findings.claim: Bind the print once with Shader.SetGlobalTexture. Declare it at file scope, outside CBUFFER UnityPerMaterial and NOT in Properties{}. Drive time with Shader.SetGlobalVector. Do not use MaterialPropertyBlocks for per-wall variation.
findings.detail:
Verified:
- Unity's SRP Batcher compatibility rule: the shader 'must declare all material properties in a single constant buffer named UnityPerMaterial' (built-ins in UnityPerDraw), and 'The GameObject mustn't use MaterialPropertyBlocks'.
- Shader.SetGlobalTexture: 'Global properties are used if a shader needs them but the material does not have them defined (for example, if the shader does not expose them in Properties block)'. A Properties entry would make the material's own (empty) value win.
- m_UseSRPBatcher: 1 in FrontRooms_URP.asset.
- Evidence that globals are SRP-Batcher-safe: URP 17.3's own Lit pass reads TEXTURE2D_X(_ScreenSpaceOcclusionTexture), declared at file scope (ShaderLibrary/AmbientOcclusion.hlsl line 8) and bound via cmd.SetGlobalTexture (ScreenSpaceAmbientOcclusionPass.cs line 567). It also reads $Globals uniforms such as _GlossyEnvironmentColor and _ScaledScreenParams (Input.hlsl lines 100-108).
- How to check: the 2019.2 SRP Batcher manual says 'You can see the compatibility status of a Shader in the Inspector panel'. The Frame Debugger also shows batches.

Inference:
- Keep the RenderTexture or array object identity constant (never reallocate), so the one-time global bind stays valid.
- Per-material palette (_InkColor, _PrintAmount) goes inside UnityPerMaterial, so L0, Shift and Exit share one print with different ink colours.
- Per-roll variation is computed in-shader from a world-position hash, not from MaterialPropertyBlocks.
- ShadowCaster, DepthOnly and DepthNormals don't need the print, which matches the rule that lighting and SSAO come only from the paper.

findings.topic: (a) Fully procedural pattern in the wall shader
findings.claim: A math-only pattern is seamless by construction, has zero memory cost and is exactly in sync everywhere. With analytic box filtering and band-limiting it is the most moire-proof option. But it caps the art at what can be written as math, which is weak for a Figma/After Effects student.
findings.detail:
Tileability (inference): define the pattern in tile space with integer frequencies, e.g. k chevrons per 0.75 m and m rows per 1.125 m. Phase parameters (scroll, wobble, stroke breathing) can animate freely. Parameters that change frequency must be integers or crossfaded between integer states.

Anti-aliasing (verified technique): Inigo Quilez shows analytic box filtering of procedural patterns from screen derivatives (filterable procedurals; the checkerboard is integrated across the pixel footprint). He also shows band-limiting: fade a component to its mean 'when the size of a 2π cycle is smaller than a pixel' using fwidth. For an SDF chevron that means:
- coverage = saturate(d/fwidth(d) + 0.5)
- lerp to mean coverage when the motif period is under ~2-3 px.

WebGL2: derivatives and float math are fine; keep uv*frequency in float, not half (inference).

Cost (inference, needs profiling): tens of ALU ops per wall pixel, small next to the Forward+ multi-light loop.

Morph: parameter morphs and smooth-min unions are trivial. Damask-like organic motifs are not practical as pure math; use a tiny SDF motif atlas plus procedural layout.

findings.topic: (b) Authored frames packed into a Texture2DArray
findings.claim: Texture2DArray is the most portable way to get designer-authored motion (Metal and WebGL 2.0). Frames import directly from a flipbook sheet (Texture Shape = 2D Array, Columns, Rows). Because the slice is chosen per pixel, it supports per-roll phase offsets and world-space waves, which single-RT approaches cannot.
findings.detail:
Verified:
- 'Texture arrays are supported if the platform supports one of the following graphics APIs: ... Metal (iOS, macOS) ... OpenGL ES 3.0 (Android, WebGL 2.0)'. Check SystemInfo.supports2DArrayTextures.
- Import: 'set Texture Shape to 2D Array', 'Set Columns and Rows', and 'Unity adds a texture array slice for each cell'.
- Shaders need target 3.5 (FrontRooms/Surface already uses #pragma target 3.5) and #pragma require 2darray.
- URP core 17.3 provides TEXTURE2D_ARRAY and SAMPLE_TEXTURE2D_ARRAY_GRAD for Metal and GLES3 (Metal.hlsl line 120).
- Texture2DArray.depth = slice count. Arrays can also be built with Graphics.CopyTexture.

Memory per frame (computed; MB = 10^6 B, mips add 1/3):
- 2048x3072 BC7: 8.4 MB, so 32 frames = 268 MB (too much)
- 1024x1536 R8: 2.1 MB; BC4: 1.05 MB
- 512x768 RG8: 1.05 MB, so 32 frames = 33.6 MB; BC5: 16.8 MB
- 512x768 R8 SDF only: 0.52 MB, so 32 frames = 16.8 MB

Two array fetches per wall pixel give the crossfade or morph. A 'wipe' is a per-pixel threshold against a gradient or noise (e.g. top-down along a roll, like a print run).

WebGL: the build uses WebGLTextureSubtarget.Generic ('Don't override texture compression'). Unity falls back to software decompression when a format isn't native. Uncompressed R8/RG8 at 512x768 sidesteps BC support questions (inference).

Iteration (inference): export, run the pack script, reimport, in seconds to tens of seconds.

findings.topic: SDF keyframes plus a coverage channel: morph up close, correct mips at distance
findings.claim: Store each frame as R = signed distance (0.5 = edge) and G = anti-aliased coverage. Blending neighbouring frames' SDFs gives a shape morph, and SDF thresholding stays crisp under magnification. At distance, blend to the mipmapped coverage channel, because averaging distances in mips erodes or bloats thin ink.
findings.detail:
Verified background:
- Valve's SIGGRAPH 2007 paper: low-resolution distance-field textures plus thresholding give sharp vector edges under magnification.
- Distance-field interpolation is an established morphing technique (Cohen-Or, Levin, Solomovici, ACM TOG 17(2), 1998).

Inference (needs a visual test):
- A plain linear SDF lerp morphs similar shapes well. Disjoint shapes fade or pop at mid-blend, so author neighbouring keyframes with corresponding shapes.
- Thresholding a mipped SDF is not a coverage average, hence the G channel. Blend factor k = saturate(texelsPerPixel - 1) with texelsPerPixel = max(|ddx uv|, |ddy uv|) * 512.
- Resolution: camera FOV is 76° vertical (FrontRooms3DGame.cs line 226). At 1080p the focal length is 540/tan(38°) ≈ 691 px. A 0.75 m roll spans ~518 px at 1 m and ~1037 px at 0.5 m. A 512-wide SDF is magnified at most ~2x (4x at 2160p), which the SDF edge handles. Paper fibre detail comes from the paper layer, so the print doesn't need 2048 px.

findings.topic: (c) Video, VideoPlayer and RenderTexture
findings.claim: Fastest for an After Effects user to preview, but a poor main system here. The module isn't installed. WebGL can only play from a URL, asynchronously and without frame accuracy. Seamless looping is officially described as unachievable on most platforms. One shared frame means no per-roll phase.
findings.detail:
Verified:
- VideoPlayer renders to a RenderTexture via renderMode/targetTexture, with isLooping, skipOnDrop and url.
- Sync: timeReference with VideoTimeReference.ExternalTime plus externalReferenceTime.
- Formats: macOS supports .mov/.mp4/.webm and more. 'The optimal supported video codec for most platforms is H.264'; H.265 offers higher compression on supported devices; VP8 is cross-platform.
- Web: embedded VideoClips are not supported ('Use the Video Player component's URL option instead'). Unity WebGL2 docs: VideoClipImporter can't be used on Web. 'Web doesn't support frame accuracy', playback is asynchronous, and Safari drift correction is disabled.
- Looping: a Unity A/V developer on Unity Discussions said seamless looping and a precise loop callback 'proved to be unachievable on most platforms'. Workarounds users suggested: VP8, Skip On Drop off, unscaled time, designing the loop around a 'rest' moment.

Inference:
- H.264 4:2:0 chroma and macroblocks can break exact edge equality, causing a seam. Horizontally it hides under the roll-seam shadow every 0.75 m; vertically (1.125 m) it would show. Encode the ink as luma only, at high bitrate, with sizes divisible by 16.
- Mips: test whether the VideoPlayer write triggers autoGenerateMips. Otherwise copy into a mipmapped RT and call GenerateMips().

Use: a lookdev sandbox (After Effects render, drop into StreamingAssets, see it on walls), not the shipped system.

findings.topic: (d) CustomRenderTexture simulation (reaction-diffusion, cellular automata, advected ink)
findings.claim: Good for a live 'mutating' print and seamless if the update samples neighbours with Repeat wrap (toroidal). It can be built in Shader Graph. But it isn't reproducible, needs float render targets on WebGL2, and its organic look is off-era. Use it for events, not the base print.
findings.detail:
Verified:
- Update modes OnLoad / Realtime / OnDemand. Period 0 = every frame. 'Double-buffers the texture. Each update swaps the two buffers', allowing reads of the previous result. Wrap Update Zones exist. Mipmap with Auto-generate is available.
- Hand-written shaders include UnityCustomRenderTexture.cginc and use CustomRenderTextureVertexShader.
- Shader Graph 17 has a 'Custom Render Texture' target and a 'Custom Render Texture Self' node ('the result of the previous update', generated as _SelfTexture2D).
- An old WebGL bug (CRT not updated when double-buffered) is listed as fixed in 2022.1/2020.3.
- Gray-Scott (Karl Sims): DA = 1.0, DB = 0.5, f = 0.055, k = 0.062, 3x3 Laplacian (centre -1, adjacent 0.2, diagonal 0.05).
- WebGL2 RG16F/R16F targets require EXT_color_buffer_float, Baseline since 2021.

Inference:
- Seed it from the chevron's frame 0 so the paper 'grows' out of the real pattern. Threshold the B field in the wall shader with fwidth for crisp two-ink edges.
- Cost: 512x768 x 9 taps x 4 iterations ≈ 14 M taps per update. Small on Apple Silicon but must be profiled.
- Determinism: chaotic; it diverges between Metal and WebGL and with frame rate unless iterations are tied to a fixed tick. All walls still match because they share one texture.

findings.topic: (e) Offscreen 2D stage rendered into a RenderTexture
findings.claim: The best route for freeform, timeline-style motion graphics from Figma. A UI Toolkit panel can render straight into a RenderTexture, and the project already imports Figma-style SVGs as VectorImages. A dedicated URP camera works too but costs a full camera render. Rive is a designer-friendly alternative that renders to a RenderTexture on Metal and WebGL.
findings.detail:
Verified:
- PanelSettings.targetTexture: 'Specifies a Render Texture to render the panel's UI on. This can be used to display UI on a 3D geometry'. In linear projects use GraphicsFormat.R8G8B8A8_SRGB; this project is linear (m_ActiveColorSpace: 1).
- URP 17 render requests: UniversalRenderPipeline.SingleCameraRequest with the destination set to a RenderTexture, submitted via RenderPipeline.SubmitRenderRequest. Supports on-demand renders, e.g. at 12 fps for a stop-motion feel.
- Rive's Unity runtime: Metal on Mac, WebGL, Unity LTS 2021+ including Unity 6, URP integration, output usable as a material texture.

Inference:
- Tileability is not automatic. Any element crossing an edge must be duplicated at ±W/±H (3x3 wrap copies), as in a Figma 'clip content' frame.
- Mips: set useMipMap and call GenerateMips() after each panel update; test whether auto-generation fires.
- Cost is mostly CPU (a camera or panel update). Throttle updates.
- A single 'now' frame means no per-roll phase, unless a ring buffer copies each update into a Tex2DArray slice with Graphics.CopyTexture (check SystemInfo.copyTextureSupport on WebGL).
- Rive is a third-party dependency; editor licensing was not researched.

findings.topic: (f) Compute shader writing a RenderTexture
findings.claim: Works on Metal, but WebGL2 has no compute shaders and WebGPU is experimental in 6000.3. A compute path would need a duplicate fragment or CustomRenderTexture fallback, and nothing in this print needs scatter writes.
findings.detail:
Verified:
- Unity lists compute support for Metal on macOS/iOS, DX11/12, Vulkan, GL 4.3 and GLES 3.1 (no WebGL2). Check SystemInfo.supportsComputeShaders at runtime.
- The 6000.3 WebGPU page: 'WebGPU is currently experimental and not supported by all browsers and devices'.
- RenderTextureDescriptor.enableRandomWrite is for SM5-level random writes.

Inference: everything a print needs (per-pixel update, neighbour reads) fits the CustomRenderTexture or plain-fragment model, which runs on WebGL2.

findings.topic: Mipmaps and anisotropic filtering for live render targets
findings.claim: Any RenderTexture source (c, d, e, f) must enable useMipMap and either autoGenerateMips or an explicit GenerateMips(), and set anisoLevel. Otherwise grazing-angle walls down a 20 m corridor will shimmer and moire, which the static texture avoids today with mips plus aniso 16.
findings.detail:
Verified:
- autoGenerateMips: 'Mipmap levels are generated automatically when this flag is set', requires useMipMap, and runs after rendering into the RT completes and the active target switches.
- GenerateMips() needs useMipMap = true and autoGenerateMips = false.
- RenderTextureDescriptor has dimension (Tex2DArray), volumeDepth, useMipMap, autoGenerateMips, graphicsFormat and sRGB.

Inference on cost:
- 1024x1536 RGBA8 is 6.3 MB, 8.4 MB with mips. Building the chain each update reads about 6 MB and writes about 2 MB, negligible on Apple Silicon.
- A double-buffered RG16F simulation at 1024x1536 is about 12.6 MB (16.8 MB with mips). At 512x768 it is a quarter of that.
- For a mask-only print, use R8_UNorm, linear. The UI Toolkit path forces RGBA8 sRGB.

findings.topic: Repetition breakup: a 3 m supertile vs per-roll offsets
findings.claim: A 4-roll (3 m) supertile coincides exactly with the 3 m maze cell, so it hides the 0.75 m repeat but not the module repeat, and costs 4x pixels. Per-roll hashed offsets (time phase and/or vertical drop) are free and break repetition better. Sampling must use derivatives from the continuous UV, and the hash period must be 4 rolls (keeps the module rule) or 256 rolls (192 m, breaks it).
findings.detail:
Verified wallpaper practice: straight match, half-drop (the next strip drops by half the repeat) and random match are standard. A per-roll vertical drop is therefore period-plausible, and vertical repeats are already 'free' in LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.

Verified shader practice: Inigo Quilez's texture-repetition article says the custom gradients 'must come from the original repeating UV mapping'. Use textureGrad / SAMPLE_TEXTURE2D_ARRAY_GRAD with ddx/ddy of the unshifted UV, or floor()-based offsets produce 1-px mip seams on every roll line.

Inference / project rule:
- hash(strip & 3) keeps 'every 3 m wall module looks the same' (TileAlign) while desyncing the 4 rolls inside a cell.
- hash(strip & 255) is rebase-safe but makes modules differ. That is an owner decision (visual chat, with map chat informed).
- A time-phase offset doesn't move the pattern spatially, so door and opening alignment is untouched.
- A world-space wave (frame offset = -distance(posWS, origin) * k, quantised per roll) gives 'a change sweeping down the corridor'. It is deterministic and only possible in (a) or (b).
- The existing 8 m and 12.8 m macro wear already breaks the 3 m rhythm and must stay static on top of the print.

findings.topic: Determinism and sync across all walls
findings.claim: (a) and (b) are pure functions of world position and a CPU clock, so they are exact, rebase-safe and identical on Metal and WebGL. (c), (d), (e) and (f) share one live texture, so all walls match each other but not the game clock. (c) is not frame-accurate on Web; (d) and (f) are not reproducible.
findings.detail:
Inference, built on the verified API behaviour above:
- Drive (a)/(b) from a C# double clock wrapped modulo the loop length, published as a global vector. This allows pause, rewind, speed-up on events and a later sync with FMOD cues without float drift.
- Avoid relying on _Time.y for long sessions; float precision degrades slowly.
- The video item is verified: 'Web doesn't support frame accuracy', with asynchronous playback.
- (e) is deterministic only if the stage animation is advanced from the same global clock rather than its own timer.

findings.topic: Authoring tools for a Figma / After Effects-level student
findings.claim: Figma Motion (open beta) exports MP4, WebM, GIF and SVG (plus Lottie/dotLottie), but not PNG sequences. After Effects can render tile-sized PNG sequences, with seams checked via Offset or Motion Tile. Houdini Copernicus has a seamless Tile Pattern node and SDF shape generators.
findings.detail:
Verified:
- Figma help 'Export animations from Figma': choose MP4, WebM, GIF or SVG; set resolution, frame rate and quality. 'Figma Motion is currently in open beta'. PNG sequences are not listed.
- After Effects: Offset ('Shift Center To') and Stylize > Motion Tile ('Tile Center') wrap a layer for seamless loops; keyframe shifts must be divisible by the tile size (ProVideo Coalition).
- SideFX: the Copernicus Tile Pattern node in Seamless mode makes 'the generated pattern ... always tileable'; Copernicus is a GPU image network with tileable generators and SDF shapes.

Inference:
- For keyframe arrays, the simplest Figma flow is static frames: one frame per keyframe, exported as PNG or SVG. Motion between them comes from the shader's SDF lerp.
- For true timed motion, use After Effects to a PNG sequence, or Figma Motion to MP4 and extract frames (e.g. with ffmpeg) before packing.

findings.topic: Comparison at a glance
findings.claim: Overall ranking for FrontRooms: (b)+(a) hybrid > (e) UI Toolkit or Rive > (a) alone > (c) video (sandbox only) > (d) CustomRenderTexture (events only) > (f) compute.
findings.detail:
Inference; WebGL2 status is from the verified facts above.

**(a) Procedural**
- Tileability: by construction
- Moire handling: best (analytic filtering)
- Memory: 0
- GPU: ALU
- Authoring: math only
- Iteration: live parameters
- Per-roll phase: yes
- WebGL2: yes

**(b) Texture2DArray**
- Tileability: authored, then validated
- Moire handling: hardware mips plus aniso
- Memory: 8-34 MB at 512x768 x 32 frames
- GPU: 2-4 fetches per pixel
- Authoring: Figma or After Effects
- Iteration: export, pack, import
- Per-roll phase: yes
- WebGL2: yes

**(c) Video**
- Tileability: authored, but codec edges can seam
- Memory: small file plus one RT
- GPU: hardware decode, copy, mips
- Authoring: easiest from After Effects
- Iteration: fastest
- Per-roll phase: no
- WebGL2: URL only, not frame-accurate; loop hiccups

**(d) CustomRenderTexture**
- Tileability: toroidal by construction
- Memory: about 13-17 MB at 1024x1536 RG16F
- GPU: N passes per update
- Authoring: Shader Graph or HLSL
- Iteration: live parameters
- Per-roll phase: no
- WebGL2: needs EXT_color_buffer_float; not reproducible

**(e) 2D stage**
- Tileability: wrap copies by hand
- Memory: one RGBA8 RT, 8.4 MB at 1024x1536 with mips
- GPU: a camera or panel render (CPU-heavy)
- Authoring: SVG from Figma, or Rive
- Iteration: live
- Per-roll phase: no
- WebGL2: yes

**(f) Compute**
- Like (d), but no WebGL2 support.

recommendations: PRIMARY: build the print as a Texture2DArray of ink keyframes (R = SDF with 0.5 as the edge, G = anti-aliased coverage), 512x768 per 0.75 x 1.125 m tile, 16-32 frames, linear, mips on, aniso 16, Repeat, uncompressed RG8 (or BC5 if WebGL support is confirmed). Sample it in FrontRooms/Surface's ForwardLit pass only, just after the albedo fetch (line 185) and before macro wear (line 194). Pick frames from a global clock, blend neighbouring frames' SDFs for a morph, anti-alias with fwidth up close and switch to the G coverage at distance. Apply ink as albedo *= lerp(1, _InkColor, ink*_PrintAmount). Do not touch nTS, smoothness or cavity.

Bind it once from a small visual-chat-owned driver (e.g. Assets/Scripts/Rendering/FrontRoomsPrint.cs): Shader.SetGlobalTexture(_FR_Print), plus Shader.SetGlobalVector(_FR_PrintClock) every frame from a wrapped C# double clock. Declare _FR_Print and _FR_PrintClock at file scope, outside UnityPerMaterial and NOT in Properties{}. Put the per-material _InkColor and _PrintAmount inside UnityPerMaterial. Never use MaterialPropertyBlocks. Confirm 'SRP Batcher: compatible' in the shader Inspector and the batch grouping in the Frame Debugger.

Split Tools/lookdev/gen_surfaces.py wallpaper() (visual chat) into two outputs:
- An ink-free paper set (Wallpaper_Paper_A/N/S). Remove the 0.9*blur(ink) height term, the +0.07*ink smoothness term and the -0.10*ink cavity term. Albedo becomes the ground colour. Keep the seam shadow, fibre, mottling, blots and foxing.
- A print set whose frame 0 is today's `ink` mask turned into an SDF, so the stopped clock reproduces the current look.
Add a validator that checks left/right and top/bottom edge equality in every frame, and frame 0 vs frame N for the loop.

Give the print sheet its own folder and import rule (e.g. Resources/Surfaces/Print/), because the existing postprocessor caps everything under /Resources/Surfaces/Textures/ at 4096 px and CompressedHQ. An 8x4 sheet of 512x768 frames = 4096x3072 (32 slices). Set Texture Shape = 2D Array, Columns 8, Rows 4, sRGB off, mips on, aniso 16.

Repetition breakup:
- Default to a per-roll time-phase offset hashed from strip = floor(U/0.75) with period 4 (strip & 3). This keeps the 'every 3 m module looks the same' rule while desyncing rolls.
- Offer period 256 (strip & 255, rebase-safe at 192 m) only if the visual and map owners accept modules looking different.
- Always sample with SAMPLE_TEXTURE2D_ARRAY_GRAD using ddx/ddy of the continuous UV.
- Skip a 3 m supertile unless a specific multi-roll motion is designed; it repeats exactly with the maze cell and costs 4x.

Add one gameplay hook: a global 'wave' (origin, speed, strength) that offsets the frame by distance, quantised per roll. Entities, light-flicker bursts or (later, with the sound chat) FMOD cues can then send a pattern change down a corridor deterministically.

Authoring workflow for the student:
1. In Figma, make a 750x1125 frame (1 px = 1 mm) with Clip content. Draw the motif in black on white. Duplicate any shape that crosses an edge at ±750 or ±1125. Keep a 3x3 instance preview to check seams.
2. Make one frame per keyframe (K0-K15), with corresponding shapes between neighbours so the SDF morph reads well. Export PNG at 2x (1500x2250) or SVG.
3. For timed motion, use After Effects instead: a 1500x2250 comp at 30 fps with the loop length as a whole number of frames; check seams with Offset (Shift Center To = half the comp size) or Motion Tile at 300%; render a greyscale PNG sequence with no paper texture and no lighting.
4. Run the pack script (SDF plus coverage, downsample to 512x768, 8x4 sheet), reimport, and scrub _FR_PrintClock in Play mode. Colours stay in the material palette, not in the frames.

FALLBACK A (freeform motion): render a UI Toolkit panel (UIDocument + PanelSettings.targetTexture, R8G8B8A8_SRGB, useMipMap + GenerateMips after each update, anisoLevel set) built from Figma SVGs (built-in 6.3 importer) with 3x3 wrap copies. Animate it from the same global clock and bind it to the same global name. Evaluate the Rive Unity runtime as the designer-tool variant. Accept the loss of per-roll phase, or add a Tex2DArray ring buffer filled with Graphics.CopyTexture.

FALLBACK B (no assets): a procedural chevron in the shader. Integer chevrons per 0.75 m roll, SDF triangle-wave bands, fwidth anti-aliasing, and a band-limit fade to mean coverage when a period drops under ~3 px. It uses the same clock, hash and wave plumbing.

Use VideoPlayer only as a lookdev sandbox, and only if the owner agrees to add com.unity.modules.video. Use a CustomRenderTexture reaction-diffusion only for scripted 'mutation' events seeded from frame 0 and thresholded into two inks. Do not build anything on compute, because of WebGL2.

Before committing, profile in the Editor on the target Mac and in a WebGL2 build:
- wall-pass cost with 2 vs 4 array fetches
- RG8 vs BC5 on desktop browsers
- whether the UI Toolkit or VideoPlayer writes trigger autoGenerateMips
- grazing-angle shimmer at 10-20 m down a corridor under ForceEnable (Standalone) and per-texture (WebGL) anisotropy
open_questions: Should the print keep a fixed 1990 vocabulary (a chevron family with anomalies: flat inks, two-ink registration), or allow freeform motion? The answer decides between the keyframe array (b) and a live 2D stage (e).

Is desyncing rolls acceptable under LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC's TileAlign rule ('every 3 m wall module looks the same')? Should the hash period be 4 rolls or 256? This needs the visual chat's decision, with the map chat informed.

Will the visual chat accept splitting gen_surfaces.wallpaper() into an ink-free paper set plus a print SDF? This changes how the current static wallpaper's normal and smoothness read, because the ink emboss and sheen go away.
Is WebGL2 a shipping target or just a demo? If it ships, which browsers and GPUs must be supported? That decides BC5 vs uncompressed RG8, and whether a float-target CustomRenderTexture is allowed.
What should drive print changes in gameplay: a constant slow loop, entity proximity, the light-flicker system, or audio cues? Syncing with FMOD would need a shared clock agreed with the sound chat.
Should Exit_Wallpaper and L0_Wallpaper_Shift share the same animated print with different palettes, or have their own frame sets?
Is a third-party runtime (Rive) acceptable, and what are the Rive editor's licensing terms? Not researched.

Unverified in Editor: does a VideoPlayer or UI Toolkit panel write into a mipmapped RT trigger autoGenerateMips, and does Graphics.CopyTexture into a Tex2DArray slice work on WebGL2 for a ring-buffer variant?
What is the actual GPU budget? The Mac model is unknown, and all cost figures here are estimates that need profiling.

code.title: Wall shader additions (sketch for FrontRooms/Surface ForwardLit; visual-chat owned)
Global print driver (sketch; visual-chat owned)

verdicts.claim: wallpaper() in Tools/lookdev/gen_surfaces.py bakes the ink into height/normal (0.9*blur(ink,1.2), line 68), smoothness (+0.07*blur(ink), line 70), cavity (-0.10*ink, line 71) and albedo (duotone, line 47).
verdicts.evidence: gen_surfaces.py line 47 is the duo np.where, line 68 is height = .18*weave + .9*blur(ink,1.2) + ..., line 70 is smooth = .20 + .07*blur(ink,1.0) ..., line 71 is cav = 1 - .35*seam_shadow/.20 - .10*ink. wallpaper_cold() (line 75) calls the same function, so Exit_Wallpaper is affected too.

verdicts.claim: Thresholding today's ink array at 0.5 and converting it to an SDF gives a frame 0 that, with an albedo *= lerp(1,_InkColor,ink) tint, reproduces the current static look exactly when the clock is stopped.
verdicts.evidence: ink = clip((0.92-lum)/0.35,0,1) is a continuous value, not a binary mask. Albedo is a three-stop duotone (ground->mid->deep), plus keep_hue (0.16 / 0.10) chroma carried over from the CC0 source and a cream lift where lum > 0.90 (lines 44-50). A binary SDF plus a single multiplicative _InkColor cannot reproduce the mid-tone band, the source hue or the cream highlight.
verdicts.correction: The stopped clock gives an approximation of today's look, not an exact match. For a close match, either store a continuous ink value (coverage in G) and use a 3-stop palette ramp (ground/mid/deep/cream as material colours) instead of one multiplicative tint, or keep the print in a colour (RGB) channel. Lighting stays paper-only either way.

verdicts.claim: The SRP Batcher stays unaffected because the global print texture is declared outside UnityPerMaterial and outside Properties. Per-wall variation must never use MaterialPropertyBlocks. Confirm 'SRP Batcher: compatible' in the shader Inspector.
verdicts.evidence: Unity's 6000.3 SRP Batcher page lists 'The GameObject mustn't use MaterialPropertyBlocks' as a GameObject requirement. FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs lines 764-769 already give every shell renderer whose material has _CeilingHeight a MaterialPropertyBlock (props.SetFloat(CeilingHeightId, ceilingWorldY); r.SetPropertyBlock(props)). LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC §5 documents this: _CeilingHeight is set 'with a MaterialPropertyBlock (shell only, never props)'. Shader-level compatibility (UnityPerMaterial CBUFFER at shader line 52) is real, and the global-texture pattern matches URP 17.3 (AmbientOcclusion.hlsl line 8, SSAO pass line 567).
verdicts.correction: Adding a global texture does not change batching. However, the wallpaper shell renderers already use MPBs, so under Unity's documented rule they are not SRP-batched today. 'Shader Inspector says compatible' does not prove the walls batch, and the frame debugger will show it. 'Never use MPBs' is already violated by map-chat code. That is an existing condition, not something the print introduces.

verdicts.claim: Shader.SetGlobalTexture globals are used only when the material does not define the property (e.g. it is not in the Properties block).
verdicts.evidence: The doc says verbatim: 'Global properties are used if a shader needs them but the material does not have them defined (for example, if the shader does not expose them in Properties block).'

verdicts.claim: Wall UVs are world-planar metres/_TileSize. Wallpaper tile = 0.75 x 1.125 m. The rebase shifts only Z by multiples of 192 m. Vertical repeats are 'Free' in LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC §5. TileAlign = Cell, with the comment 'every 3 m wall module looks the same'.
verdicts.evidence: Shader lines 157-162 (PlanarFrame, t = normalize(cross(up,n))) and line 183 (uv = metres/_TileSize * _BaseMap_ST.xy + ST.zw). RenderSetup line 32 has Roll = .75f, and lines 272/273/278 have tile = (Roll, Roll*1.5f). RoomStream line 52 has RebaseThreshold = 192f, and lines 942-944 shift camera Z by floor(z/192)*192. Spec line 84: 'Free: vertical repeats'. ModuleUnits line 20 is the TileAlign comment. Two caveats: the uv also includes _BaseMap_ST, which the sketch ignores, and the _FR_MESH_UV variant exists (used only by Prop_* materials).

verdicts.claim: (a)/(b) driven by world position plus a CPU clock are rebase-safe, including the world-space 'wave' (frame offset = -distance(posWS, waveOrigin)*k).
verdicts.evidence: RebaseIfNeeded moves the camera and rooms by -192 m in Z (RoomStream lines 937-950). The roll hash with period 4 or 256 is rebase-safe. But the sketch's distance(positionWS, _FR_PrintWave.xyz) uses a fixed world-space origin. After a rebase the same wall sits 192 m closer to or further from that origin, so its frame offset jumps (pops) unless the driver also shifts the wave origin.
verdicts.correction: Either have the print driver subscribe to the rebase and subtract the same shift from _FR_PrintWave.z, or wrap the distance term modulo a 192 m-compatible period. The rebase applies to the title stream ('Title stream rebase: 192 m', spec §5).

verdicts.claim: FrontRoomsSurfaceTextureImporter forces maxTextureSize 4096 and CompressedHQ under /Resources/Surfaces/Textures/, with mips, Trilinear, aniso 16, Repeat, sRGB only for _A/_E, and does not touch textureShape. Standalone defaults to quality 5 (Ultra, aniso ForceEnable) and WebGL to 3 (High, aniso per-texture).
verdicts.evidence: RenderSetup lines ~619-640 match this, with no textureShape assignment. QualitySettings.asset m_PerPlatformDefaultQuality has Standalone: 5 and WebGL: 3. Level 3 'High' has anisotropicTextures: 1, and level 5 'Ultra' has anisotropicTextures: 2. The Texture.anisoLevel doc confirms range 0-16, 0 = off under Forced On, 1-9 -> 9, and independent mip/aniso control on Metal/Vulkan/OpenGL.

verdicts.claim: Texture arrays are supported on Metal and WebGL 2.0. A flipbook imports via Texture Shape = 2D Array plus Columns/Rows, one slice per cell. Shaders need target 3.5 and #pragma require 2darray. URP core 17.3 defines SAMPLE_TEXTURE2D_ARRAY_GRAD for Metal and GLES3.
verdicts.evidence: The API list ('Metal (iOS, macOS) ... OpenGL ES 3.0 (Android, WebGL 2.0)') and the import steps are confirmed verbatim. Core Metal.hlsl line 120 and GLES3.hlsl lines 131/156 define the GRAD macro. The use-in-shader page gives #pragma target 3.5 OR #pragma require 2darray as alternatives, not both.
verdicts.correction: Because FrontRooms/Surface already has #pragma target 3.5, adding #pragma require 2darray is optional, not required.

verdicts.claim: The Video module is not in the manifest. UI Toolkit/PanelSettings/VectorImage are already used with Unity 6.3's built-in SVG importer. The Vector Graphics package is needed only for Sprite/uGUI.
verdicts.evidence: manifest.json has no com.unity.modules.video. FrontRooms3DGame.cs uses UIDocument/PanelSettings/VectorImage and loads Brand/*.svg. The .svg.meta files use ScriptedImporter script guid 0000000000000000e000000000000000 (built-in). The Vector Graphics 3.0 manual says the package is needed only for the Sprite and uGUI import types.

verdicts.claim: On Web, embedded VideoClips are unsupported (URL only), 'Web doesn't support frame accuracy', playback is asynchronous, and Safari drift correction is disabled. A Unity A/V developer said seamless looping is unachievable on most platforms.
verdicts.evidence: webgl-video page quotes match. In the Discussions thread, DominiqueLrx ('A/V developer at Unity') says 'Seamless looping and a precise callback on loop point proved to be unachievable on most platforms' (looping AND a precise callback together).

verdicts.claim: PanelSettings.targetTexture renders UI to a RenderTexture for 3D geometry, using R8G8B8A8_SRGB in linear projects. The project is linear.
verdicts.evidence: The doc text matches. ProjectSettings.asset has m_ActiveColorSpace: 1 (Linear).

verdicts.claim: Rive's Unity runtime renders to a RenderTexture on Metal and WebGL, supports Unity LTS 2021+ including Unity 6, and has URP integration.
verdicts.evidence: The cited page confirms Metal (Mac/iOS), WebGL and 'Unity LTS versions from 2021 upwards (including Unity 6)'. It does not mention RenderTexture output or URP integration.
verdicts.correction: The RenderTexture and URP parts are unverified from the cited source. Check the rive-unity GitHub README and WEBGL.md before relying on it.

verdicts.claim: Figma Motion (open beta) exports MP4, WebM, GIF, SVG plus Lottie/dotLottie, not PNG sequences.
verdicts.evidence: Confirmed by the Figma help page, including the open-beta sentence. The same page also says exports over 1920x1080 or 30 FPS need a paid plan, which the report omits. The recommended 1500x2250 frame exceeds 1080 in height.
verdicts.correction: The Figma Motion -> MP4 route at 1500x2250 needs a paid plan, or a smaller export such as 750x1125, which is still fine for a 512x768 SDF. Static per-keyframe PNG/SVG export is unaffected.
