verdicts.evidence: The compute intro lists DX11/12, Metal, Vulkan, GL 4.3, GLES 3.1 and consoles, with no WebGL. The WebGPU page says 'WebGPU is currently experimental and not supported by all browsers and devices.'

gaps: Existing MaterialPropertyBlocks on wall shells (FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs lines 764-769, _CeilingHeight) mean the walls are already outside the SRP Batcher under Unity's GameObject rule. The report's SRP Batcher argument and its 'never use MPBs' rule ignore this. The print could even use that same per-renderer MPB if per-block variation were wanted, at no extra batching cost.

The print is not a binary chevron today. ink is continuous, and albedo uses a 3-stop duotone plus keep_hue source chroma plus a cream lift. A single _InkColor multiply and a 0.5-threshold SDF lose the mid-tone and hue, so the 'exact frame 0' promise is false. A palette ramp (ground/mid/deep/cream in UnityPerMaterial) indexed by continuous coverage is needed.
The wave term is not rebase-safe (it uses a fixed world origin in distance()). The driver must listen for RoomStream's 192 m Z rebase and shift the wave origin.

fwidth(sdf) across a roll boundary where the per-roll frame index or phase changes will spike and produce a thin AA line on every roll seam. It is partly hidden by the baked seam shadow, but should be called out. Computing fwidth on a per-roll-continuous value or clamping it is safer.
The sketch computes print UV as metres/_TileSize and ignores _BaseMap_ST, so print and paper drift apart if anyone sets a material ST.

Removing ink from height/smoothness/cavity removes the current emboss and sheen variation that reads as printed ink. The paper layer then needs its own emboss/weave that does not follow the motif. That is a visible look change the visual chat must sign off on, which the report mentions only as an open question.

The 4096 maxTextureSize cap applies to the source sheet before slicing (inference, not verified in Editor). The report's 8x4 of 512x768 = 4096x3072 fits, but this was not checked against Unity's actual behaviour for 2D Array shape with Default texture type and CompressedHQ.
Memory figures and GPU cost are unprofiled estimates. No check was made of whether 2 extra array fetches matter in the Forward+ loop on the user's specific Mac or in WebGL2.

No mention of the per-fixture flicker lighting interacting with a changing print. Because lighting is paper-only, light flicker and print change are independent, but perceptually a moving albedo under flickering light may read as noise. This is a design question, not a technical one.

report.summary:
Direction: how the print changes across space and with game state. Short answer: it can be built, and almost all of it can be built without touching map or audio files. The game already exposes the hooks it needs as public API: FrontRooms3DGame.MapRunStarted gives the map world and the Relay; there are public map events plus PassageBetween, DoorBetween, CellOf, ZoneOf and IsBuilt; the Relay exposes Position, State, SeesPlayer and StateChanged.

Proposed architecture:
- One CPU component owned by the visual chat (FrontRoomsPrintDirector, in Rendering/*).
- It writes a few shader globals: a wrapped clock float4, an 8-slot event array, and two 64x64 world-anchored state textures with one texel per 3 m cell.
- It runs in RenderPipelineManager.beginCameraRendering. There it works out which cells the camera can see (conservative frustum plus grid-portal test) before the frame is drawn. A cell that comes into view mid-change is snapped to the nearer end state before it is ever shown, so no pop is visible.

The shader finds per-cell state by nudging each wall-face pixel 0.5 m along its normal into the room it faces, then reading texel (cell & 63). It computes the roll-strip index as floor(u/0.75) from the existing PlanarFrame u. Hashes use only world-periodic indices: strip & 255 and wall line & 63, both with a 192 m period. That way the existing 192 m root and rebase rule moves nothing. The motion layer feeds albedo and an optional phosphor emission only. Normal, smoothness and cavity stay on the paper layer. SSAO (geometric normals in the DepthNormals pass) and shadow passes never see the print.

Project facts that change the brief:
- buildRadius is 2, so 5x5 chunks (40x40 cells, 120 m) are built, not 3x3. The 3x3 ring is only the ReadyAround(1) gate. A 64x64 toroidal texture (192 m) covers this with no scrolling.
- Fog is ExponentialSquared at 0.014, so a wall at 20 m is about 93% unfogged. "Unseen" must come from frustum, portals and the 46 m far plane, not fog.
- There is no sprint-noise event and no public lamp-level API.
- The sound director's Tension value is private.

Those gaps are the only places that need the map chat or the sound chat, and each has a workaround that needs no edits.

findings.topic: Hooks available today (no edits needed)
findings.claim: Everything the print director needs to read is already public. A rendering-side component can subscribe exactly the way the sound director does.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED in code:
- FrontRooms3DGame exposes `public static event Action<FrontRoomsMapWorld, FrontRoomsMapHunter> MapRunStarted`, plus `MapRunEnded` and `PlayerClimbed(Vector3)`.
- FrontRoomsMapWorld events: DoorMoved, GlassBroken, DoorBroken, KeyTaken, GlassHold(pos, progress), GlassHoldReleased, DoorLocked (all Vector3 or GridCoord).
- FrontRoomsMapWorld queries: PassageBetween(a,b) returns Open/Wall/ClosedDoor/Glass. DoorBetween(a,b) returns a Door with public open, progress and broken. Also CellOf(world), CellCenter, ZoneOf (ZoneInfo id/height/theme), IsBuilt(cell), InStartArea, SightDistance, and Cache.IsBuilt(chunk) / Cache.Get(chunk).revision. Get is side-effect free for a cached chunk.
- FrontRoomsMapHunter exposes Position (world feet), Heading, Moving, State (HunterState: Dormant/Listen/Hunt/Search/Chase/BreakDoor/Wander), StateTime, SeesPlayer, Released, and the events StateChanged, DoorBlow(Vector3) and Caught.
- FrontRoomsSoundDirector already uses this pattern (OnMapRunStarted, then subscribing to the map and Relay events).

INFERENCE: a print director in Assets/Scripts/Rendering (visual chat) can therefore drive every spatial and game-state effect below without editing map or audio files. The only gaps are noted in other findings.

findings.topic: Streamed area and state-texture sizing (corrects the brief)
findings.claim: The live streamed area is 5x5 chunks (40x40 cells, 120 m), not 3x3. A 64x64 toroidal state texture (1 texel per 3 m cell, 192 m period) covers it with no scrolling, because 64 cells is exactly ModuleUnits.WorldPeriod.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED:
- FrontRoomsLevel0.asset has buildRadius 2. The tooltip says "2 = 5 x 5 chunks, 120 m across".
- The 3x3 ring is only ReadyAround(1), the door-open gate.
- Camera far plane = SightDistance = buildRadius*24-2 = 46 m. Lamps light within 16 m (3 m fade); 1 lamp in 3 casts Soft shadows within 9 m.
- The map root always sits on a multiple of 192 m (64 cells).

INFERENCE (design): index the texture by `cell & 63`. Because the root is a multiple of 64 cells, world cell & 63 equals map cell & 63, so the texture is anchored to the world and never needs to scroll with the ring. With 40 live cells in a 64 period, live cells never alias. Clear a chunk's 64 texels when it is dropped (detect by polling map.IsBuilt or Cache revision).

Use two textures:
- A, discrete, point-sampled: current variant, previous variant, progress, transition kind.
- B, continuous, bilinear: local light, phosphor charge, agitation/wave, zone phase.

At RGBA32 that is 2 x 16 KB uploaded per frame.

findings.topic: Which cell a wall pixel belongs to
findings.claim: Each wall face should read the state of the cell it faces, found by sampling at positionWS + normalWS*0.5. Then the two sides of one 0.16 m wall can carry different states, matching the rooms they are in.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED:
- Walls are centred on cell lines, 0.16 m thick (WallHalf 0.08).
- Cell (x,y) covers X [3x,3x+3), Z [3y,3y+3).

INFERENCE (geometry check):
- A +X face at x=3k+0.08 probes x=3k+0.58, giving cell k.
- The -X face at 3k-0.08 probes 3k-0.58, giving cell k-1. Correct on both sides.
- Columns (0.6/0.9 m on 6 m-grid corners) and opening reveals resolve the same way.

Title stream rooms (start area) are not map cells. Leave their texels neutral (0) so they show the base print. Only L0_Wallpaper, L0_Wallpaper_Shift and Exit_Wallpaper should take the motion layer. Office walls are drywall.
sources: Documentation/LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md §2 (lines on Wall 0.16 centred, cell coverage)

findings.topic: Roll strips from world coordinates
findings.claim: Strip index = floor(u / 0.75 m), where u is the existing PlanarFrame tangent coordinate. Seams fall on world multiples of 0.75 m on both faces of every wall, and every 3 m cell line is also a strip seam (4 strips per cell).
findings.detail:
VERIFIED:
- PlanarFrame sets t = normalize(cross(up, n)) for walls and u = dot(positionWS, t). So u = -z for +X faces, +z for -X faces, +x for +Z faces and -x for -Z faces. The sign flips, but |u| seams land on the same world lines.
- gen_surfaces.py wallpaper() draws the roll-seam shadow and lift at the texture's x=0/W edges, so the baked seam already sits on these strip boundaries.
- Tile is 0.75 x 1.125 m.

INFERENCE (design), per-strip parameters from a hash of the strip key:
- (a) phase lag: t_strip = t - lag*h.
- (b) half-drop slip: pattern V += 0.5 repeat on odd strips or on one chosen strip. A whole-repeat offset is invisible at rest, so an animation that ends on a whole repeat leaves no trace.
- (c) misregistration: up to ~3-10 mm V/U offset that scales with dread.
- (d) a peeling strip.

Peeling is a PAPER-layer change (seam lift in normal and cavity, or a curl mesh), not a motion-graphic change. Keep it in the paper layer so lighting stays correct.

Real precedent: wallpaper is matched straight, half-drop or third-drop between strips, and rolls must share a batch reference. A phase or variant change landing on a cell line therefore reads in-world as a different roll or print batch. That is period-plausible, and zone/region discontinuities can hide there.

findings.topic: Floating origin: hashes must be world-periodic
findings.claim: Any per-strip or per-cell hash must use indices modulo the 192 m period (strip & 255, cell or wall-line & 63). Otherwise a 192 m root offset or rebase changes every hash and reshuffles all strip phases.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED:
- Every world-projected period must divide 192 m: 0.6/1.2, 0.75, 1, 8, 12.8 and 24 m. Map roots, capture roots and origin shifts sit on 192 m multiples.
- The title stream rebases by whole multiples of 192 m (RebaseIfNeeded, TotalRebaseShift).
- Map play has no rebase today.
- Captures and tests use root 4992 m.

INFERENCE:
- 192/0.75 = 256 strips and 192/3 = 64 lines, so `strip & 255` and `line & 63` (two's complement makes negatives wrap correctly) keep every hash invariant under a 192 m shift. Any new region period (noise field, wave tiling) must also divide 192 m (24, 48, 64, 96 or 192).
- Event centres in _FR_Events are absolute world XZ. On any rebase the CPU must shift them by the same amount (subscribe to the stream's shift, or a future map-play shift event).

Precision note (computed): float32 spacing at 4096-8192 m is 2^-11 m = 0.49 mm. The paper texel is 0.75/2048 = 0.37 mm, so the 4992 m test root already sits where positionWS quantises at about 1.3 texels. Near the game's root (hundreds of metres, about 0.03 mm) this does not matter. URP does not render camera-relative.
sources: Documentation/LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC.md §5 (Roots on a 192 m multiple; Title stream rebase)

findings.topic: Global time: wrap on the CPU
findings.claim: Don't build the motion layer on URP _Time. In URP it equals Time.time since application start, it does not reset when R reloads the scene, and float precision degrades over long sessions. Send CPU-wrapped phases computed from Time.timeAsDouble instead.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED:
- Unity: _Time = (t/20, t, 2t, 3t), and time matches Time.time, "the time since the application started". Only the Built-In pipeline uses timeSinceLevelLoad.
- Unity recommends Time.timeAsDouble for precision over extended periods.
- Unity: float is the type for world positions, UVs and trig; half can be 16-bit (min16float) on some platforms.

INFERENCE (computed):
- After 1 h, float spacing is 0.24 ms. After 1 day it is 7.8 ms, enough to wreck any sin(t*120) term.
- Unbounded offsets like t*speed added to pattern UV also grow without limit.

Recipe:
- `_FR_PrintClock = (frac(now/96s), frac(now/11s), dread01, now mod 64s)`, computed in double and cast to float. Each periodic animation uses its own wrapped phase.
- Event times are sent as AGE (now - t0, computed in double), never as absolute t0.
- Do all strip and phase math in float, not half. The existing shader uses half for bands, which is fine there.
- Pause: Time.timeScale is set to 1 at line 295 of the game script. Decide whether the print freezes in pause (scaled time) or keeps breathing (unscaled).

findings.topic: Fog can't hide changes
findings.claim: With ExponentialSquared fog at density 0.014, walls at 20 m are still about 93% visible and at the 46 m far plane about 66%. So 'unseen' must come from frustum, portals and the far plane, never from fog.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED:
- FrontRoomsLook sets FogMode.ExponentialSquared with FogDensity 0.014.
- The local URP ShaderVariablesFunctions.hlsl implements factor = exp(-(density*z)^2).

INFERENCE (computed): exp(-(0.014*20)^2) = 0.925 and exp(-(0.014*46)^2) = 0.66.

MAP_GENERATION says rebuilt chunks are 'inside the fog'. What actually hides decision-2 shifts is that they are rebuilt at least 24 m away and, in practice, past the 46 m far plane (they rebuild as they re-enter ring 2). Lamps beyond 16 m are off, but the Trilight ambient (equator 0.34, 0.31, 0.22) still lights those walls visibly.

findings.topic: Change only when unobserved: which visibility source
findings.claim: Use a CPU test: breadth-first search from the camera's cell over see-through edges, keeping only cells whose box passes GeometryUtility.TestPlanesAABB, run in RenderPipelineManager.beginCameraRendering. Renderer visibility callbacks, CullingGroup and GPU readback are each worse here.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED:
- Renderer.isVisible and OnBecameInvisible count a renderer visible when it must render for shadows, and the Scene view counts in the editor.
- CullingGroup uses frustum plus STATIC occlusion culling only (a procedural maze has no baked occlusion). Its results arrive through culling, so you cannot change the scene and immediately re-query.
- TestPlanesAABB is conservative and may give false positives. CalculateFrustumPlanes has a non-allocating Plane[6] overload.
- beginCameraRendering lets code run before URP renders each camera.
- AsyncGPUReadback adds a few frames of latency. Random write from pixel shaders needs target 4.5 (ES 3.1).
- The existing shader is target 3.5 (ES 3.0). WebGL2 lacks compute.

PROJECT FACTS: shell renderers are merged per 6 m block, material and ceiling height. With 1 in 3 lamps casting soft shadows within 9 m, the blocks behind the player are often 'visible' for shadow maps, so OnBecameInvisible would rarely fire exactly where 'behind you' changes matter.

INFERENCE, recommended algorithm (conservative: false 'visible' only delays a change, false 'unseen' would cause a pop):
1. Compute planes from the game camera only (cameraType Game; skip Scene view).
2. Start at the camera's cell plus its 8 neighbours.
3. Expand into a neighbour if the edge is see-through: Open/Arch, Glass (transparent), or a Door whose open flag is set or progress > 0. Note that PassageBetween reports ClosedDoor until progress > 0.6. Also require the neighbour's box (3.2 x ceiling+slab x 3.2) to pass TestPlanesAABB.
4. Write lastSeen[cell] = now for every visited cell.

The frustum is convex and contains the eye, so any straight sight line stays inside it. This search is therefore a superset of the truly visible cells. Typical maze cost is about 100-300 cells times 6 plane tests, well under 0.1 ms. WebGL builds have no threads, but this fits on the main thread.

Optional desktop-only ground truth: a per-cell 'seen frame' UAV written by the wall shader plus AsyncGPUReadback. It accounts for furniture and door-leaf occlusion, but it is not WebGL2-compatible and has multi-frame latency. Use it only to verify the CPU result.

findings.topic: Reprinting without popping
findings.claim: Advance a cell's transition only while it has been unseen for a hold time. If the visibility pass in beginCameraRendering finds a cell newly visible mid-transition, snap it to the nearer end before the frame renders. The player's first frame of that wall is then already a clean state.
findings.detail:
INFERENCE (design):
- Hold times: tier-1 'behind you' reprint after ≥3-4 s unseen; Relay-wake reprint after ≥3 s unseen; decay back to the base print after 60-120 s, also only while unseen.
- Snapping on entry is safe only because visibility is computed in the same frame before drawing. Doing it in Update would risk a one-frame lag during fast mouse turns. At 76° vertical FOV and 16:9 the horizontal FOV is about 108° (computed).
- A second, legitimate window is a masked change (next finding): a transition allowed while visible because a light dropout hides it.
- Precedents: Layers of Fear changes rooms when you turn away. The Exit 8 makes noticing anomalies the core loop.
- Decision-2 chunk shifts (≥30 s away, rebuilt out of view) are a free, guaranteed-unseen moment. Derive the chunk's print variant from hash(chunk, revision), polled through Cache.Get(chunk).revision when Cache.IsBuilt(chunk), so the shifted room also returns with different paper.

findings.topic: Lamp flicker as a change-blindness mask
findings.claim: The existing per-fixture flicker supplies natural 'flicker' and 'mudsplash' masks. Changes made during a local dropout are hard to notice even in view, so a strip can slip while the lamp stutters.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED (research):
- Rensink, O'Regan & Clark (1997): with images alternating 240 ms and separated by ~80 ms blanks, observers take a long time to see large changes.
- O'Regan, Rensink & Clark (1999): changes timed with brief disruptions (a blink, a flicker, small 'mudsplashes' that don't even cover the change) are often missed.

VERIFIED (code), lamp temperaments rolled per cell (62% steady, 20% stutter, 10% failing ballast, 5% dead-with-blinks, 3% dim):
- Mode 1 stutters for 0.15-0.85 s, toggling 0.95/0.05, every 5-20 s.
- Mode 2 drops to 0.05 when Perlin > 0.72.
- Mode 3 blinks to 0.8 for 0.06-0.18 s every 8-28 s.
- The sound director already detects 'Tick' (level > 0.6 then < 0.15) and 'Strike' transitions, polled at 5 Hz.

INFERENCE (design): on a dropout of the cell's own lamp (or the dominant one), allow a strip slip or variant step to complete within the dark window, then freeze. Players will learn that 'when the lights flicker, the walls move', which is a readable rule. Ambient light is constant, so the drop is relative, not black. Keep these noticeable-tier only and rate-limited.

findings.topic: Light-reactive print and a phosphorescent layer
findings.claim: Compute local light per cell on the CPU from the lamp levels rather than adding a second light loop in the shader. A phosphor 'charge' per cell can then reveal a hidden glow print when lamps die. Era-correct pigment for 1990 is copper-activated zinc sulfide; strontium aluminate was only invented in 1993.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED:
- Strontium aluminate pigments were developed in 1993 by Nemoto (patented 1994). They are about 10x brighter and 10x longer-glowing than Cu:ZnS, which was the common glow-sticker pigment before.
- Lamp levels live in the private Fixture class. The only public route today is what the sound director does: scan GameObjects named 'Light' and normalise Light.intensity by the maximum seen. TickFixtures sets intensity = base*level*fade and toggles enabled.
- Trilight ambient is constant everywhere.

INFERENCE (design and data flow):
- Field.R = L_cell = own lamp level + 0.25 x the 4 neighbours (unshadowed lamps light through walls in this game anyway).
- Field.G = phosphor charge q, integrated per cell: dq/dt = kc*L*(1-q) - kd*q.
- In the shader, emission = glowInk(motion layer) x ZnS-green x q x paperCavity x paperFibre. The paper layer still 'shades' the glow by masking it.
- Physically, the glow is swamped while lit and only reads when the lamp dies.
- Contrast is limited because ambient (about 0.17 linear on mid-tone paper) never drops. The visual chat may scale bakedGI by lerp(0.35, 1, L_cell) so dead-lamp cells actually go dark. That is a lighting decision for the paper layer, not the print.
- Lamp death as a dynamic event (e.g. the Relay passing kills a lamp) does not exist yet: temperaments are fixed per cell. It would need a change in FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs (map chat file), even though LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC §4 makes flicker odds the visual chat's numbers.

findings.topic: Event wipes and ripples: straight-line vs along the corridors
findings.claim: Two mechanisms, both cheap. (a) An 8-slot global float4 array of event centres and ages for straight-line rings. (b) A CPU breadth-first search over passable edges that writes arrival time into the field texture, so a wave travels along the maze like sound.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED (code), event sources and radii:
- Relay noise radii: sprint steps 26 m, door moves 14 m, breaking glass 40 m.
- DoorBlow fires every 0.5 s while the Relay breaks a door (2.5 s total).
- StateChanged fires on Hunt/Search/Chase/etc.
- The sound director fires a RelayStinger on Hunt, Search, Chase and Lost.

VERIFIED (Unity): globals are used only when the material does not define the property. So _FR_* must stay out of the Properties block and the UnityPerMaterial CBUFFER.

INFERENCE (design):
- (a) _FR_Events[i] = (worldX, worldZ, age, strength). Ring = exp(-((d - 7 m/s*age)/1.2 m)^2) * exp(-age/1.6 s). It warps only the pattern UV (≤1 cm) or advances the pattern phase, never the normal. Cost is 8 iterations of about 10 ALU per wallpaper pixel.
- (b) On GlassBroken, Relay→Chase or DoorBroken, flood from the source cell through PassageBetween != Wall (closed doors attenuate) at 6-10 m/s. The CPU writes per-cell agitation = f(now - arrival) into Field.B each frame (4096 cells, trivial). The wall bilinear-samples it, so the wave turns corners and doesn't leak through solid walls. This reads as 'the walls carry the sound' and is more diegetic than (a).
- Shader.SetGlobalVectorArray is believed to fix the array length on first set (not confirmed on the 6000.3 page), so always set the full 8.
- Sprint has no event; the game calls relay.Noise directly at FrontRooms3DGame.cs:854. Either infer sprint from player speed (walk 3.2 vs run 5.5 m/s) or ask the map chat for a noise event.

findings.topic: Per-region phase
findings.claim: Give each zone its own print phase or program through the field texture (Field.A = zone-phase hash written per cell from map.ZoneOf). Discontinuities then fall on cell lines, which are always strip seams, and read as a different print batch.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED:
- Zones are irregular nearest-site regions crossing chunk borders.
- Where the height class changes the edge is a Wall/Door/Window, but zones of equal height can meet through open edges.
- ZoneInfo has id (site chunk), height and theme, and is pure in seed and coordinates.

INFERENCE:
- Hashing ZoneInfo.id gives a stable per-zone phase and program, e.g. Low 2.4 m zones drift faster and feel oppressive, Tall halls slower.
- Optionally hash (chunk, revision) so decision-2 shifts change the paper too.
- Use point sampling (State) for hard per-cell programme switches and bilinear (Field) for phase, so phase blends across about 3 m where zones meet in an open room.

findings.topic: Relay as a spatial driver (a print 'wake')
findings.claim: Relay.Position and State can drive both a proximity agitation field and a 'wake': cells the Relay walked through get reprinted once unseen. That gives an attentive player a diegetic trace of where it has been.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED:
- Relay.Position is world-space feet. Sight range is 12 m (ray at eye height). It wanders 6-14 cells at 80% speed.
- The sound director already leaks proximity through walls (heartbeat proximity = 1 - d/20 m regardless of occlusion; Tension mixes state weight and proximity over 30 m).

INFERENCE (design):
- Each frame: relayCell = map.CellOf(relay.Position). If it changed, set relayVisit[cell & 63] = now. After ≥3 s unseen, switch that cell to the 'Relay variant' (e.g. darker ink, slightly rotated chevron, or only misregistration if a full swap is too strong). Decay after 60-120 s, unseen.
- Proximity agitation (subliminal to noticeable): a phase jitter scaled by saturate(1 - d/20 m) x state weight, using the same weights as the sound director's Tension, so sight and sound agree.
- Balance risk: the wake is a tracking tool. Tune it as a mild tell, or show it only in the Relay's last N cells.

findings.topic: Sound coupling
findings.claim: Drive picture and sound from shared game signals (Tension, Relay state, lamp transitions) rather than metering audio output. Both are possible with the project's FMOD 2.03.15 wrapper, and a print-to-sound 'paper settle' cue needs a new FMOD event from the sound chat.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED:
- The project's FMOD for Unity is 2.03.15 (VERSION.number 0x00020315).
- Studio System.getParameterByName(name, out value, out finalvalue) exists in the local wrapper. The sound director writes the globals Tension (smoothed: rises 2/s, settles 0.5/s) and Zone every frame, but the `tension` field is private.
- RuntimeManager's debug overlay already meters output: master.getDSP(0), setMeteringEnabled(false, true), getMeteringInfo, rmslevel.
- Studio Bus.getChannelGroup and lockChannelGroup exist, so a bus such as bus:/AMB (hum and air beds) can be metered the same way.
- TIMELINE_MARKER is an event callback type.
- FrontRoomsFmod.OneShot(path, pos, params) is public static. FMOD can fail and fall back to legacy Unity audio (then nothing is set).

INFERENCE (recommendation):
- Visuals should compute their own dread from the Relay, using the same formula as Tension, or read the FMOD global with a local fallback. That keeps them deterministic and alive when FMOD fails, including on WebGL.
- For 'breathing with the hum', let the print director own one slow LFO and send it to FMOD as a new global parameter (e.g. PrintPulse) that the sound chat automates on HumBed. One clock, one direction.
- Print-to-sound: after a tier-1 unseen reprint finishes within about 8 m, play a quiet positional 'paper settle/rustle' at the wall centroid. Play it AFTER the change completes, so turning round reveals an already-changed (or seemingly unchanged) wall.
- Stinger sync: subscribe to the same relay.StateChanged the sound director uses, so tier-2 waves line up with RelayStinger with no cross-chat call. FMOD Studio callbacks run off the main thread (standard FMOD practice, not re-verified here), so marker callbacks must queue work to Update.

findings.topic: Transition vocabulary in world space
findings.claim: Use five world-space transitions built from print-shop failure modes, which suits the 1990 era lock better than digital glitches. Each one only blends old and new motion-layer ink in albedo.
findings.detail:
INFERENCE (design; timings are starting points for playtest):
1. Fibre dissolve, 'ink soaking through': new where fibreNoise < p. The noise comes from the paper layer, e.g. the unused MaskMap A channel (gen_common documents A as unused, B as wet mask). A 2-4 mm darker 'wet front' sits at the threshold. 0.6-1.2 s masked or unseen; 2.5-4 s as a visible event.
2. Strip wipe, 'rehung': per strip, top to bottom (y > ceiling*(1-q)), each strip 0.25-0.4 s, staggered 60-120 ms by strip index. Direction runs away from the source (Relay or noise).
3. Reprint roll: a 10-15 cm vertical band sweeps along the wall at 1.5-3 m/s. Behind it is the new print; at the band, misregistration smear plus slight darkening (wet ink).
4. Strip slip (half-drop): one strip's pattern slides vertically to half a repeat over 0.3-0.8 s (eased), or instantly when masked or unseen. Sliding a whole repeat is invisible at rest.
5. Roller slip, the period-safe 'glitch': 2-8 cm horizontal slices offset by a fraction of a repeat for 1-3 frames.

Avoid RGB split and pixel blocks, which read as post-1990 digital. Continuous ambient motion: drift and breathing (below).

Rendering rule: every transition picks UV and ink for the motion layer only. normalTS, smoothness and cavity come from the paper layer untouched, so highlights and SSAO never betray the print.

findings.topic: Subtlety tiers and horror pacing
findings.claim: Three tiers, gated by a director-style intensity curve: subliminal (always on), noticeable (only unseen or masked, every 30-90 s), and event (visible, at most one per 2-4 min, on Peak), with a relax window after each event.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED: the Left 4 Dead AI Director paces through Build Up, Sustain Peak (3-5 s after intensity peaks), Peak Fade, and Relax (minimal threat for 30-45 s).

INFERENCE (design):
- SUBLIMINAL. Phase drift ≤1-2 mm/s and scale breathing ±0.3% at 0.05-0.1 Hz, amplitude scaled by dread (0.05 to 0.6). By computation, at 1080p and 76° vertical FOV one pixel at 2 m is about 2.5 mm, so 1 mm/s is about 0.4 px/s: felt over seconds, invisible in a still. Purpose: unease in Build Up and Relax; reveals no rules.
- NOTICEABLE. Unseen reprints behind you, lamp-masked strip slips, one lagging strip, the Relay wake, corridor waves from door moves. Purpose: paranoia and anomaly literacy (Exit 8), and teaching that noise disturbs the walls too, which reinforces the stealth loop (noise also draws the Relay).
- EVENT. Relay to Chase: a wave from the Relay along corridors at about 8 m/s, which also points toward the threat. Glass break: strongest wave. Door-break blows: one flinch per 0.5 s blow. A lamp dying in view: phosphor reveal. Each 1.5-4 s, aligned to the audio stinger.
- After an event, force subliminal-only for 30-45 s (the Relax analogue). Freeze everything on Caught. While the player is still in the title stream rooms, allow only subliminal.

findings.topic: Sandwich integrity: what the print can and cannot touch
findings.claim: In the current shader, SSAO and shadow passes take nothing from albedo or the normal map. If the motion layer writes only albedo (and optional emission), lighting, reflections and AO stay driven by the paper layer as the user wants. Today, though, the pattern ink is baked into the paper normal, smoothness and cavity, so it must be removed from those maps.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED:
- FrontRoomsSurface's DepthNormals pass uses URP's generic DepthNormalsPass.hlsl. With no _NORMALMAP keyword it writes the interpolated geometric normal, so SSAO (depth-normals source) ignores both the paper normal and the print.
- ShadowCaster uses ShadowCasterPass.hlsl (depth only).
- gen_surfaces.wallpaper() currently writes height = ... + 0.9*blur(ink), smoothness + 0.07*ink and cavity - 0.10*ink, so the static chevron is in the lighting today.

INFERENCE:
- Regenerate the paper set without the ink terms (visual chat, Tools/lookdev). The motion layer then multiplies paper albedo only.
- Spatial and state effects must never write normalTS or smoothness. The one exception is deliberate paper-layer states (peel or seam lift, damp), which change the physical paper.
- MaterialPropertyBlocks make a renderer SRP-Batcher-incompatible, and the map already sets _CeilingHeight per shell renderer through an MPB. Driving the print with globals and textures adds no further batching cost.

findings.topic: Cost and WebGL2
findings.claim: The whole spatial and state layer is small enough for Metal and for WebGL2: about 0.1-0.3 ms CPU, about 32 KB texture upload per frame, and about 2 texel fetches, an 8-step loop and 1-2 extra pattern samples per wallpaper pixel.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED:
- Target 3.5 = OpenGL ES 3.0 with integers. Target 4.5 adds compute and randomwrite.
- Texture2D.Apply copies the whole texture (fine at 64x64).
- The WebGL build profile has no WebGL threads.
- RaycastCommand batches raycasts as jobs (only for an optional ray-based visibility refinement; on WebGL they run without worker threads).

INFERENCE (estimates, unprofiled):
- CPU: BFS 100-300 cells x TestPlanesAABB < 0.1 ms; 64x64 field update < 0.1 ms in plain C#; event BFS only on events.
- GPU per wallpaper pixel: State Load + Field bilinear sample + 8-event loop (about 80 ALU) + strip hash (about 10 ALU) + old/new ink samples during transitions + one fibre sample. That is small next to the Forward+ light loop with shadowed spots, and 4x MSAA shades per pixel, not per sample.
- The paper texel (0.37 mm) is far below screen resolution at 2 m (about 2.5 mm/px), so the motion layer can be authored at about a quarter of the paper's resolution.
- AsyncGPUReadback and UAV 'seen buffers' are desktop-only extras.

recommendations: Visual chat builds one component, FrontRoomsPrintDirector (Assets/Scripts/Rendering). It subscribes to FrontRooms3DGame.MapRunStarted/MapRunEnded and RenderPipelineManager.beginCameraRendering (game camera only). It owns: the two 64x64 RGBA32 Repeat textures (_FR_PrintState point, _FR_PrintField bilinear), _FR_PrintClock (CPU-wrapped phases from Time.timeAsDouble), and _FR_Events[8] (sent as ages). None of these go in the shader Properties block or UnityPerMaterial, because a material value overrides a global.

Add an include (e.g. FrontRoomsPrint.hlsl) to FrontRooms/Surface used only by the wallpaper materials. It resolves the cell (positionWS + 0.5*normal, & 63), the strip (floor(u/0.75)), and a periodic strip key (strip & 255, line & 63, facing), then outputs a motion-layer UV, ink mix and optional emission. It must never write normalTS, smoothness or cavity. Keep the math in float.

Make 'unseen' a CPU grid-portal BFS plus TestPlanesAABB, computed per frame before rendering. Treat Glass and any door with open || progress > 0 as see-through, and always include the 3x3 cells around the camera. Snap mid-transition cells that come into view. Don't use OnBecameInvisible or fog for this.

Ship the tiers in order: (1) subliminal drift and breathing scaled by a locally computed dread value (the same formula as the sound director's Tension); (2) unseen reprints, the Relay wake, and lamp-dropout strip slips; (3) corridor-following event waves on Relay→Chase, GlassBroken and DoorBlow, with a 30-45 s relax lockout afterwards.

Regenerate the paper set without ink in height, smoothness and cavity (Tools/lookdev/gen_surfaces.py, visual chat). Put a paper-fibre threshold field in MaskMap A (currently unused) for the fibre dissolve.

Map chat dependencies (their files; ask, don't edit). (a) Optional: a read-only lamp API, e.g. `float LampLevel(GridCoord)` or a `FixtureChanged(Vector3, float level)` event, instead of scanning 'Light' GameObjects like the sound director. (b) A noise event for sprint steps (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:854 calls relay.Noise directly); a workaround is to infer sprint from player speed. (c) Optional ChunkBuilt/ChunkDropped(GridCoord, revision) events, since polling Cache.Get(chunk).revision works today. (d) If lamps should die as events (the Relay passing, etc.), that is new logic in FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs. (e) If map play ever gets an origin shift, it must stay a 192 m multiple and raise an event so print event centres can be shifted. (f) Note in LEVEL_MODULE_SPEC §5 that the print's state-texture period (64 cells) and strip period (0.75 m) also divide 192 m.

Sound chat dependencies (their files). (a) Expose `public float Tension` on FrontRoomsSoundDirector, or accept that the print reads the FMOD global with a local fallback. (b) Add an event such as event:/Ambience/PaperSettle (params Size = strips changed, Distance) to Tools/audio/fmod_frontrooms.py SPEC, SoundIds and the banks. (c) Optional: a global parameter (e.g. PrintPulse) that the print director drives, automating HumBed. (d) Optional: timeline markers in RelayStinger events to sync tier-2 waves, with callbacks queued to the main thread. (e) Optional: raise the lamp Tick/Strike detections as a C# event so visual slips and audio ticks share one trigger.

Verify with a capture tool in the existing pattern (visual chat's editor folder): log per-frame counts of visible cells, cells that changed while flagged visible (must be 0), and snaps on entry. Run it on the autopilot seeds (2554, 20388) with -autopilotSeed. Also test at the 4992 m capture root to see texel quantisation of the motion layer.
open_questions: Should the print be allowed to leak information through walls, through Relay proximity agitation and the Relay wake? The heartbeat already does this through walls, but the wake makes the Relay trackable. How strong a tell does the design want?
Is the 'flicker = walls move' rule a learnable mechanic the game wants to teach, or should lamp-masked changes stay unexplained?
Should the print freeze in pause (scaled time) or keep breathing (unscaled)? The game sets Time.timeScale = 1 at FrontRooms3DGame.cs:295; how pause is implemented was not checked.
Will the map chat add a map-play origin shift? Today there is none, so a long straight walk only drifts a few km, but the verification root at 4992 m already sits in the 0.49 mm float band.
Should the title stream rooms (start area, not map cells) get any motion layer? They read neutral texels by default.
Is ZnS:Cu green phosphor in wallpaper ink acceptable for the 1990 era lock as an anomaly? Strontium aluminate (1993) would be anachronistic.
What is the WebGL2 frame budget? No profiling was done here; all costs above are estimates.
