report.summary:
Verdict: the sandwich idea fits this renderer, and the risks can be checked one at a time. In FrontRooms/Surface the print only has to change s.albedo. With metallic 0, URP's specular colour is a constant 0.04 whatever the albedo (BRDF.hlsl), so highlights, normals, cavity and SSAO can come from the paper layer alone. The project has no baked GI, no realtime GI, no light probes and no APV (all three scenes, the pipeline asset and the scripts were checked). Ambient is a fixed trilight SH set by FrontRoomsLook. So an animated albedo can never fall out of step with bounce light, because there is no bounce light. The shader's DepthNormals pass writes only the geometric normal, so SSAO ignores both layers.

Five real risks, in order of size:
(1) Aliasing and moiré. The print's dominant stripe period is about 37.5 mm (20 cycles per 0.75 m roll, measured from Wallpaper_Chevron_A.png). That passes screen Nyquist about 6 m down a corridor at grazing angles. MSAA does not anti-alias texture content and there is no TAA, so any live print must have mips plus anisotropic filtering. Neither is on by default for a RenderTexture, and the editor (High: aniso per texture) and the Standalone build (Ultra: aniso forced on) behave differently.
(2) Lighting does not yet ignore the pattern. gen_surfaces.py bakes the ink into height (0.9*blur(ink)), smoothness (+0.07) and cavity (-0.10). The paper maps have to be regenerated without ink, and that slightly changes today's look under raking light.
(3) Precision. _Time is a float, and the maze never rebases: the map root can sit 24 × 192 m = 4.6 km out, where UVs lose about 1 texel. Animation phase and scroll should be wrapped in double on the CPU and passed in as globals.
(4) Photosensitivity. A moving or contrast-reversing stripe field that fills the screen, on top of the fluorescent flicker the game already has.
(5) Process. The SRP Batcher, shader variants, sampler limits and WebGL2 each need specific choices.

Expected GPU cost (my estimate, to be measured): +1 to 3 texture samples per wall pixel, a few percent of the per-pixel work at most, since each shadowed light already does 16 compare taps at High soft shadows. A small R8 RenderTexture updated only when it changes is negligible. Recommended order: P0 static split with parity tests; P1 a global print source (prefer a Texture2DArray flipbook, use a RenderTexture only for generative content); P2 transitions done in the wall shader, reusing the macro noise it already samples; P3 game-state drive with hysteresis. Each step is gated by lookdev A/B, light-sweep, grazing-moiré and autopilot GPU-time tests.

findings.topic: Lighting setup: baked GI / probes / APV
findings.claim: The project is realtime-only. There are no lightmaps, no realtime GI, no light probe groups and no APV, and ambient is a fixed trilight SH. Animating the albedo cannot cause a bounce-light mismatch.
findings.detail: VERIFIED in the project: all 3 scenes have m_EnableBakedLightmaps: 0 and m_EnableRealtimeLightmaps: 0 with the built-in empty LightingDataAsset. No LightProbeGroup or ReflectionProbe exists in any scene or script; the only hit is RoomStream setting reflectionProbeUsage Off. FrontRooms_URP.asset has m_LightProbeSystem: 0 (legacy), with every APV/scenario option off. FrontRoomsLook.ApplyAmbient sets Trilight colours plus DynamicGI.UpdateEnvironment, so the ambient is a constant, not derived from surfaces. FrontRooms/Surface also has no Meta pass, which is what the lightmapper reads albedo from, so a future bake would not see the print either. INFERENCE: the one remaining coupling is artistic. The ambient constants are tuned for beige paper and carpet; a print whose mean luminance or hue moves far (measured today: mean linear Y = 0.433, RGB about 0.54/0.44/0.14) will look under- or over-filled. Keep a print 'albedo budget' (for example mean Y within ±15%) rather than driving DynamicGI.UpdateEnvironment every frame, whose cost was not measured.

findings.topic: Specular is independent of albedo (metallic 0)
findings.claim: In URP 17.3, InitializeBRDFData sets brdfSpecular = lerp(kDielectricSpec, albedo, metallic). With _Metallic = 0 on the wallpapers, highlight colour and strength do not depend on the print at all; only the diffuse term does.
findings.detail: VERIFIED in Library/PackageCache/com.unity.render-pipelines.universal@37e0d4fc2503/ShaderLibrary/BRDF.hlsl lines 82-97. This makes the core sandwich test exact: with _BaseColor tint = 0 (spec only), frames rendered with print A and print B must be bit-identical. The custom shader does not declare `multi_compile_fragment _ DEBUG_DISPLAY`, which URP Lit.shader does (line 167), so INFERENCE: the URP Rendering Debugger material views probably will not work on FrontRooms/Surface. Tests should use material tint and global-texture swaps instead.

findings.topic: Ink currently leaks into lighting inputs
findings.claim: The current paper maps encode the print. In wallpaper(), height = 0.18*weave + 0.9*blur(ink) + 0.40*fib + seam, so ink is the largest term of the normal map; smoothness gets +0.07*blur(ink); cavity gets -0.10*ink. Highlights and ambient occlusion therefore trace the chevron today.
findings.detail: VERIFIED in Tools/lookdev/gen_surfaces.py lines 68-71. With _OcclusionStrength 0.8, ink areas get about 8% less indirect light, and ink is about 35% glossier (0.27 vs 0.20). To meet the rule that lighting comes from the texture layer, the paper _N and _S must be regenerated without the ink terms. Fibre, weave, mottling, blots, foxing and the roll-seam shadow and lift stay in the paper. INFERENCE: this changes the static look under raking light, so P0 needs two targets. P0a keeps today's maps and only splits the albedo, for exact parity. P0b uses ink-free paper maps, with a measured diff and an art sign-off. Design option: keep a static 'embossed vinyl' relief of the original chevron in the paper, visible only under raking or flickering light as a ghost of the old print. The print also contains a hue residual, (big - lum)*keep_hue, from the pink and slate bands of the source, plus a cream highlight lift. A single-channel ink mask loses these unless a second channel or an RGB print is used.

findings.topic: SSAO / DepthNormals pass
findings.claim: The shader's DepthNormals pass includes URP's generic Shaders/DepthNormalsPass.hlsl, which outputs only the interpolated geometric (vertex) normal. It samples no normal map, and no UVs except for alpha test. Neither the print nor the paper normal map affects SSAO.
findings.detail: VERIFIED in package source: DepthNormalsFragment writes NormalizeNormalPerPixel(input.normalWS); uv is only declared under _ALPHATEST_ON. SSAO is configured with Source = 1 (depth normals) in FrontRooms_URP_Renderer.asset. Consequence: AO is identical whatever the print, which suits the sandwich, but the paper emboss is also absent from AO (radius 0.45 m, so it doesn't matter). RISK to avoid: switching to LitDepthNormalsPass.hlsl to get normal-mapped AO. Under _NORMALMAP it samples _BumpMap with mesh UV0 (TRANSFORM_TEX(input.texcoord, _BaseMap)), which is wrong for world-projected walls. If that is ever wanted, write a custom fragment that reuses PlanarFrame and samples only the paper normal.

findings.topic: Anti-aliasing: MSAA only, no TAA
findings.claim: The cameras use AntialiasingMode.None plus pipeline 4x MSAA. MSAA does not fix texture or shading aliasing, so the print has to be band-limited through mips and anisotropic filtering. TAA cannot be combined with MSAA and would ghost a texture-space animation.
findings.detail: VERIFIED: FrontRoomsPostStack.ConfigureCamera sets data.antialiasing = AntialiasingMode.None; FrontRooms_URP.asset has m_MSAA: 4. URP docs: MSAA 'does not fix shader aliasing issues such as specular or texture aliasing'; TAA uses motion vectors and cannot be used with MSAA. INFERENCE: URP motion vectors encode geometry and camera motion only, so a scrolling or morphing print would get no reprojection and TAA would smear it. Stay on MSAA plus filtered textures, and author the motion graphics band-limited, with anti-aliased edges and no features under 2 to 3 texels of the print canvas.

findings.topic: Measured pattern frequency and the aliasing distance
findings.claim: The print is dominated by vertical stripes with a period of about 37.5 mm (FFT peak at 20 cycles per 0.75 m roll; harmonics 14/22/26), and a vertical zigzag of about 0.56 m (2 cycles per 1.125 m). At 1080p with the 76° vertical FOV, the stripes reach Nyquist about 13 m away head-on and about 6 m down a 3 m corridor at grazing angles.
findings.detail: MEASURED read-only on Assets/Resources/Surfaces/Textures/Wallpaper_Chevron_A.png (2048x3072). Luminance p5/p50/p95 = 0.19/0.47/0.60 (linear), max per-pixel gradient 0.33, so the stripes are high-contrast. INFERENCE (arithmetic): screen density is 1080/(2·tan38°·d) ≈ 691/d px/m, so one stripe period covers about 25.9/d px head-on; a side wall 1.5 m away, 6 m ahead, is foreshortened by about sin14° = 0.24, giving about 1 px per period. Any print source without mips and anisotropic filtering will moiré within a few metres. Wagon-wheel (reversed motion) begins when per-frame displacement exceeds P/2: horizontal scroll faster than 1.125 m/s at 60 fps or 0.56 m/s at 30 fps. For smooth motion, keep horizontal stripe motion at or below P/4 per frame: about 0.28 m/s if the game can drop to 30 fps. macRetinaSupport = 1 means Standalone may render at 2x, which doubles the safe distances but quadruples the pixel cost.

findings.topic: Anisotropic filtering: quality levels differ between editor and build
findings.claim: The editor runs Quality 'High' (anisotropicTextures 1 = per texture), while Standalone defaults to 'Ultra' (anisotropicTextures 2 = Forced On) and WebGL to 'High'. A RenderTexture or array left at its default aniso level gets no anisotropic filtering in the editor and in WebGL, but forced aniso (minimum 9) in the Mac build. Tests must cover both.
findings.detail: VERIFIED: ProjectSettings/QualitySettings.asset has m_CurrentQuality: 3 (High) and m_PerPlatformDefaultQuality Standalone: 5 (Ultra), WebGL: 3. Surface textures are imported at aniso 16, trilinear, Repeat (FrontRoomsSurfaceTextureImporter). Unity docs: with Forced On, anisoLevel 1-9 is raised to 9 and 0 disables aniso; Metal, Vulkan and OpenGL control mip and aniso filtering independently. Also VERIFIED: the autopilot perf baseline therefore runs at the editor's 'High', not the shipped 'Ultra'.

findings.topic: Sampler state and RenderTexture settings
findings.claim: On Metal, sampling the print with sampler_BaseMap gives it the base map's trilinear, aniso-16, Repeat sampler for free and adds no sampler slot. On WebGL2 (GLES-style coupled samplers) the print texture's own wrap, filter, aniso and mip settings apply, so set them explicitly anyway.
findings.detail: VERIFIED (Unity docs): the 'Sample a texture in HLSL' page says separate samplers can be reused across textures; separate samplers aren't available on OpenGL ES; inline samplers ('sampler_trilinear_repeat_aniso8') work only on D3D11/12 and Metal; D3D11 allows 128 textures but only 16 samplers. Apple's Metal limits list 16 sampler entries per function. RenderTexture: mips need useMipMap = true; autoGenerateMips runs when the active target switches, otherwise call GenerateMips() manually. VERIFIED absence: no Unity doc found that states RenderTexture's default wrapMode, so set Repeat explicitly and assert it in a test. INFERENCE: use a canvas whose sides divide evenly, such as 1024x1536, so box-filtered mips stay periodic; 3072-tall NPOT chains end in odd sizes (3→1).

findings.topic: SRP Batcher: CBUFFER vs globals vs MaterialPropertyBlock
findings.claim: Put shared, time-varying print state in global shader properties, and per-material palettes and strengths in UnityPerMaterial. Never use an MPB, and never call SetX on the shared .mat assets. The map shell renderers are already SRP-Batcher-incompatible because FrontRoomsMapWorld gives each one an MPB for _CeilingHeight.
findings.detail: VERIFIED (docs): a GameObject 'mustn't use MaterialPropertyBlocks' to be SRP-Batcher compatible; the MPB page warns of a likely performance drop in URP. Material properties must be in one UnityPerMaterial CBUFFER; FrontRooms/Surface declares it in HLSLINCLUDE, so the layout is shared by all four passes, and new per-material fields must go there and in Properties. Global values are used only when the shader does not declare the property in its Properties block, so the global names must stay out of Properties and differ from material property names. Changing renderer.sharedMaterial changes the project asset too, so in Play mode in the editor it would dirty L0_Wallpaper.mat and fight FrontRoomsRenderSetup's regeneration. VERIFIED (project): FrontRoomsMapWorld.AddRenderer (lines 763-768) calls SetPropertyBlock with _CeilingHeight on every shell renderer whose material has that property, which includes every FrontRooms/Surface material. The streamed title rooms do not, so their walls still batch. INFERENCE: with about 25 chunks the lost batching is cheap. A later fix, owned by the map and visual chats, would be per-height-class material instances or a world-Y-derived ceiling.

findings.topic: Precision: world position near 192 m multiples, and the maze never rebases
findings.claim: The stream rebases by 192 m, but the maze does not. The map root is a multiple of 192 m picked by a ring search of up to 24 rings (≤ 4608 m), and the player then walks freely. At 4.6 km the planar UV (x/0.75 ≈ 6144) has a float32 step of 2^-11 tile, about 1 texel of a 2048-px map. Scroll offsets must not add further unbounded growth.
findings.detail: VERIFIED: FrontRoomsRoomStream.RebaseThreshold = 192; FrontRooms3DGame.MapRootFor loops ring 0..24 with root = (a·192, 0, b·192); no rebase code exists in Assets/Scripts/FrontRoomsMap. ModuleUnits.WorldPeriod = 192, where 192/0.75 = 256 and 192/8 = 24 and 192/12.8 = 15 are integers. The 1.125 m paper drop does not divide 192, which is safe only because wall V comes from world Y. Unity's HDRP docs explain that absolute float precision falls off away from the origin. INFERENCE (IEEE-754 arithmetic): ulp(uv) is 1.2e-4 at 1 km (0.25 texel at 2048 px) and 4.9e-4 at 4.6 km (1 texel). This already applies to today's paper and is not yet visible. Fixes: wrap any scroll in double on the CPU into [0,1) tile units, and optionally subtract a CPU anchor, a multiple of 192 m nearest the camera, before PlanarFrame. Since 192 m is a whole number of tiles for every period, the pattern does not move. On WebGL and mobile, `half` may become mediump (Common.hlsl turns real/half into min16float when SHADER_API_MOBILE is defined), so UVs and time must never be half.

findings.topic: Precision: _Time over long sessions
findings.claim: _Time is a float4 (t/20, t, 2t, 3t) and Time.time is a float; Unity recommends Time.timeAsDouble for precision over long running time. Drive the print from a CPU-side double phase, wrapped and passed as a global. This also makes the print pausable, scrubbable, game-state driven and deterministic in captures.
findings.detail: VERIFIED: the built-in shader variables doc defines _Time as float4 (t/20, t, t*2, t*3); the Time.timeAsDouble doc says it 'offers more precision than a float ... particularly over extended periods'. INFERENCE (arithmetic): float seconds have a step of 0.24 ms at 1 h, 3.9 ms at 10 h and 7.8 ms at 24 h. At 24 h a 16.7 ms frame step is quantised into 15.6/23.4 ms jumps, so motion judders. Edit-mode editors stay open for days, so the lookdev and Scene views would show this first. In half precision, t ≥ 1024 s has a 1 s step.

findings.topic: Temporal artefacts with the post stack
findings.claim: Film grain (0.22) is re-seeded every frame from Time.frameCount. Chromatic aberration (0.06; Office 0.03) puts RGB fringes on high-contrast stripes at the screen edges. Bloom (threshold 1.05) and lens distortion (-0.04, which resamples the image) can turn a moving stripe field into coloured shimmer and pulsing halation near troffers.
findings.detail: VERIFIED: URP PostProcessUtils.ConfigureFilmGrain calls Random.InitState(Time.frameCount) for the grain offset. FrontRoomsRenderSetup.EnsurePost sets grain Medium3 0.22, CA 0.06, bloom threshold 1.05 and intensity 0.55, lens distortion -0.04. INFERENCE: grain masks low-amplitude print changes, so subtle transitions need about 2-3% luminance steps to read. A/B captures rendered inside one synchronous Capture() call share a frameCount and therefore the same grain, which makes them comparable without disabling post.

findings.topic: Photosensitivity
findings.claim: A full-screen, high-contrast stripe pattern that moves, oscillates or reverses contrast, added to the independently flickering fluorescents, is a recognised seizure risk. It needs a flash/pattern check and a reduce-motion option.
findings.detail: VERIFIED: WCAG 2.2 'Three Flashes or Below Threshold' defines ≤ 3 general or red flashes per second, area limited to 25% of any 10° field, approximated as 341x256 px. Wikipedia notes that static stripe patterns can trigger seizures and that full-field stimuli are riskier. The ITC/Ofcom guidance, quoted via search because the PDF returned 403, treats regular patterns of more than 5 light-dark stripe pairs as potentially harmful when they change direction, oscillate, flash or reverse contrast, and exempts patterns that flow smoothly in one direction. INFERENCE: a wall at 1.5 m shows about 100 stripe pairs, so prefer one-direction drift, morphs and palette shifts over contrast reversal, and keep reversals under 3 Hz.

findings.topic: GPU cost of 1-3 extra samples on Apple Silicon/Metal
findings.claim: Expected: small next to the existing per-pixel cost, but it must be measured, because the autopilot is frame-capped and has no GPU timing.
findings.detail: VERIFIED context: wall fragments today do 5 material fetches (base, normal, mask, 2x macro), plus SSAO, plus, per shadowed point light at High soft shadows, 16 compare taps (Shadows.hlsl SampleShadowmapFilteredHighQuality uses fetchesUV[16]). The pipeline asset has m_SoftShadowQuality: 3 and an additional shadowmap of 4096. Application.targetFrameRate = 60 (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:291), and the research audit notes 'GPU headroom is unknown because the frame rate is capped and no GPU timing was captured'. FrameTimingManager supports GPU time on Metal on macOS and is always active in the editor and development builds; it is unsupported on WebGL. INFERENCE: at 1080p with about 50% wall coverage (about 1 M fragments; 4x MSAA still shades about once per pixel away from edges), +1 to 3 aniso-trilinear fetches is roughly +1 to 3 M fetches per frame. That is a few percent of wall fragment work, on the order of 0.05-0.3 ms, rising toward 4x on a Retina player and at grazing aniso. Packing the paper tone into _MaskMap.B/A makes P0 cost +1 fetch, or +2 with a palette ramp.

findings.topic: Cost of a shared RenderTexture updated every frame
findings.claim: An R8 1024x1536 canvas (about 1.6 MB, about 2.1 MB with mips), rewritten and mip-generated each frame, costs well under 0.1 ms and about 0.1 GB/s. A 2048x3072 RGBA8 canvas is about 33 MB per update with mips, about 2 GB/s at 60 Hz. That is still small against the 68-400 GB/s of M1 to M3 Max, but there is no reason to pay it.
findings.detail: INFERENCE from the arithmetic, using unified-memory bandwidth figures from Wikipedia's Apple M3 article (M3 Max 300/400 GB/s; M1 68 GB/s). Each update on a TBDR GPU also costs an extra render pass and a blit-encoder mip pass. Recommendations: update only when the print changes, at a capped 12-30 Hz (period-plausible limited animation), with linear R8 for masks (sRGB only if storing colour), useMipMap on with manual GenerateMips after each write, wrap Repeat, Trilinear, anisoLevel 16. Memory, INFERENCE: today each print run is about 3 x 8 MB at BC7/BC5 2048x3072 with mips. Sharing one paper N/S across Lobby, Shift and Exit, with print runs becoming palette rows, would retire Wallpaper_Chevron_Cold_A/N/S (about 24 MB).

findings.topic: Print source options
findings.claim: Preferred source: a pre-rendered Texture2DArray flipbook (BC4 mask, mips baked offline) sampled with a global frame index and blend. Use a runtime RenderTexture only for parametric or generative content. Avoid VideoPlayer and compute.
findings.detail: VERIFIED: texture arrays are supported on Metal and OpenGL ES 3.0 (WebGL 2.0); VideoClips aren't supported on Web, only the URL option, without frame accuracy; compute shaders are listed for D3D11/12, Metal, Vulkan, GL 4.3 / ES 3.1, with WebGL absent. Custom Render Texture has Realtime/OnDemand update modes and double buffering, but its docs do not state WebGL support. INFERENCE: video's 4:2:0 chroma and codec blocking will smear 37.5 mm coloured stripes, and it adds decode cost. A flipbook allows per-roll phase offsets (a different slice per 0.75 m roll, hidden by the existing seam shadow), which a single shared RenderTexture cannot. URP Decals are a poor fit: they need DBuffer support in the custom shader and full-screen MRTs at 4x MSAA.

findings.topic: WebGL2 constraints
findings.claim: WebGL2 is a secondary target. It supports Texture2DArray and render-to-texture blits, but has no compute, no VideoClip assets, no separate or inline samplers, no GPU frame timing, and possibly mediump half precision.
findings.detail: VERIFIED: the WebGL2 page says WebGL 2.0 needs explicit precision qualifiers, warns against unneeded shader variants because Web memory is limited, and says AA is supported on 'most (but not all)' browser/GPU combinations. FrameTimingManager does not measure GPU time on WebGL. The build profile is 128 MB initial / 1 GB max memory at a 1280x720 canvas. INFERENCE: R8 is colour-renderable and filterable in WebGL2, so an R8 RenderTexture with GenerateMips should work; confirm with a WebGL build. Anisotropic filtering depends on the EXT_texture_filter_anisotropic extension being present.

findings.topic: Shader variants and stripping for _FR_PRINT
findings.claim: Use `#pragma shader_feature_local_fragment _FR_PRINT`, enabled by FrontRoomsRenderSetup on the 3 wallpaper materials. Do runtime on/off through a global mix value, not keyword switching. Use dynamic_branch if runtime keyword toggling is ever needed. Avoid multi_compile_local, which doubles every ForwardLit variant.
findings.detail: VERIFIED: shader_feature compiles only the combinations used by materials in the build and is meant for material-based branching; multi_compile is for C#-driven runtime branching and multiplies variants; `#pragma dynamic_branch` turns keywords into uniform bools that must be tested with `if`, not `#if`. A stripped variant falls back to the 'closest' one. Project: _FR_MESH_UV is multi_compile_local because FrontRoomsOfficeFurniture creates FrontRooms/Surface materials at runtime (EnableKeyword("_FR_MESH_UV")). Those never need the print, and the wallpaper .mat assets live in Resources, so they ship with the build. The _fragment suffix keeps variants out of the vertex stage; the ShadowCaster, DepthOnly and DepthNormals passes need no keyword.

findings.topic: Composite order and roll registration
findings.claim: The wear stack (macro tone and dirt, stains, floor and ceiling grime), the paper fibre and the seam shadow must multiply on top of the print. Otherwise the print reads as a projection. Motion that crosses roll seams breaks real wallpaper's pattern registration.
findings.detail: VERIFIED: the shader applies macro wear after the base sample (FrontRoomsSurface.shader lines 189-223); the generator puts the seam shadow and lift at every tile edge (x = 0, W). INFERENCE: albedo = print(ink, palette) x paperTone x _BaseColor, then the existing wear lines unchanged. Whether motion stays inside rolls or flows across seams is an art decision; per-roll phase offsets look physically plausible.

findings.topic: Documentation drift
findings.claim: VISUAL_RESEARCH_LOOKDEV.md §2 still says the tiles 'divide the 256 m rebase' and wallpaper = '256/373 m'. The code uses a 192 m rebase and a 0.75 x 1.125 m roll.
findings.detail: VERIFIED by comparing Documentation/VISUAL_RESEARCH_LOOKDEV.md lines 104-109 with FrontRoomsRenderSetup.cs (Roll = .75f, tile Roll x Roll*1.5) and ModuleUnits.WorldPeriod = 192. This belongs to the visual chat's documentation. Fix it before writing the print spec so the period maths in the new doc is right.

recommendations: ARCHITECTURE: composite in the existing ForwardLit fragment of FrontRooms/Surface (owned by the visual chat). The print writes only s.albedo. Paper-only _BaseMap (tone: fibre, mottling, foxing, blots, seam), _BumpMap and _MaskMap drive the normal, smoothness, cavity and seams. Do not use extra geometry layers, transparent overlays or URP decals. They would double lighting cost and need depth-normals or DBuffer support.

Regenerate the paper maps in Tools/lookdev/gen_surfaces.py without the ink terms: height without 0.9*blur(ink), smoothness without +0.07*ink, cavity without -0.10*ink. Export the print separately: an ink mask plus the hue residual (keep_hue) and the cream lift. Either use an RGB print, or R8G8 ink plus band with a 256xN palette ramp whose rows are Lobby, Shift and Exit. That lets Wallpaper_Chevron_Cold_* be retired.

BINDING: put per-material values (_PrintStrength, _PaletteRow) in the UnityPerMaterial CBUFFER and in Properties, written by the SurfaceDef table so a RenderSetup re-run keeps them. Make shared, animated state global (Shader.SetGlobalTexture/Vector with cached property IDs, set once per frame), using names that are not in Properties. Keep a static _PrintMap on the material as the fallback, and blend toward the live global by _FR_PrintParams.w. An unset global float is 0, so edit mode, captures and builds without the driver still show the static print. No MaterialPropertyBlocks, and no SetX on sharedMaterial.

SAMPLING: sample print textures with sampler_BaseMap (same Repeat, trilinear, aniso 16; no new sampler slot on Metal). Still create every live texture with useMipMap = true, wrapMode = Repeat, filterMode = Trilinear and anisoLevel = 16, because WebGL uses the texture's own sampler. Prefer a 1024x1536 canvas with sides that divide evenly; the print needs less resolution than the paper because the fibre detail lives in the paper.

SOURCE: P1/P2 should use a Texture2DArray flipbook (BC4 or BC7 slices, mips baked offline) indexed by global frameA/frameB/blend. Use a RenderTexture only for generative content: R8, updated only when changed, at 12-30 Hz, GenerateMips after each write. Avoid VideoPlayer (Web needs URL sources, and chroma subsampling smears the stripes) and compute shaders (not on WebGL2).

TRANSITIONS (P2): compute them in the wall shader as a dissolve between two slices thresholded by the macro noise already sampled (m1/m2). That needs no extra fetch, is world-anchored and continuous across walls. Add a global wavefront (position plus radius) for spreading events. Phase-offset per 0.75 m roll (hash of floor(u)) so the seam shadow hides the offset; never offset per 3 m cell, which would cut a continuous wall.

TIME AND PRECISION: accumulate print time in double on the CPU from Time.timeAsDouble or a game clock, wrap it to the flipbook length and scroll to [0,1) tile units, and pass it as a float global. Never use _Time for the print, never use half for UV or time, and keep horizontal stripe motion ≤ 0.28 m/s (P/4 per frame at 30 fps). If T5 fails at far map roots, subtract a CPU anchor that is a multiple of 192 m before PlanarFrame.

VARIANTS: add `#pragma shader_feature_local_fragment _FR_PRINT` to ForwardLit only, enabled by FrontRoomsRenderSetup on L0_Wallpaper, L0_Wallpaper_Shift and Exit_Wallpaper. Turn it on and off at runtime through the global mix, not by toggling the keyword. Check the shader Inspector shows 'SRP Batcher: compatible' after adding the CBUFFER fields. Keep the generic DepthNormalsPass.hlsl include.

ACCESSIBILITY: add a 'reduce wall motion' option that freezes the print or limits it to slow one-direction drift and palette fades. Cap contrast reversals of the stripe field below 3 Hz, and treat the print and the fixture flicker as one combined stimulus in testing.

VALIDATION P0 (static split, matching the current look). Build the two-layer path with today's chevron as a static print. T1 Parity: extend FrontRoomsLookdevCapture (visual chat) to render each of the 10 existing shots twice inside one Capture() call, legacy material vs split material. One call means a shared Time.frameCount and therefore identical grain; the Hunter is already hidden. P0a (today's N/S) passes with wall-region mean |Δ| ≤ 1/255 and 99th percentile ≤ 4/255 per channel. P0b (ink-free N/S) produces a diff report plus an art sign-off of a 3-light raking sheet.

VALIDATION P0 lighting independence. T2 Light sweep: a new capture with a fixed camera 1.2 m from a Lobby wall and one point light swept through 12 positions, from 0.3 m grazing to frontal. Use an HDR ARGBHalf RenderTexture with post off. (a) Specular only (_BaseColor tint 0 on a test material instance): print A vs print B must be bit-identical, proving no ink leaks into normal, smoothness or cavity. (b) Irradiance invariance: with constant prints of 0.25 and 0.75 via a global texture swap, I0.75 − I0.25 must equal 2·(I0.25 − I_spec) within 1e-3 relative. (c) Wear-over-print: stain and grime ratio masks must match between prints A and B.

VALIDATION aliasing. T3 Grazing-moiré: camera at 1.62 m eye height, 1.5 m from a straight 24 m wall, yawed so the wall spans 3°-30°; capture 60 frames static and 60 animating at the planned speed. The reference is the same view rendered at 4x resolution and box-downsampled. Pass when the print path's error against the reference is ≤ 1.1x the error of today's static texture, with no new low-frequency FFT peaks in the wall region and no wagon-wheel reversal. T4: repeat T3 under Quality High (editor and WebGL default) and Ultra (Standalone, forced aniso), and in a WebGL build. Confirm in the Frame Debugger that live textures have mips and aniso.

VALIDATION precision and period. T5: render the same wall shot at offsets 0, +192 m, +1536 m and +4608 m (map ring 24); pass with mean |Δ| ≤ 1/255 against the origin shot and no visible seam at 0.75 m roll edges at 0.3 m distance. T6 Long session: start the print clock at 1e5 s; per-frame phase steps must be constant within 1%.

VALIDATION P1 (shared global print). Add T1-T5 with the live source (array or RenderTexture) bound globally, comparing the frozen frame 0 to P0. Scene view, lookdev and Level Designer preview cameras must show the fallback print when no driver runs. In the Frame Debugger, the stream-room wallpaper draws stay in SRP batches; the map shells stay as they are now (non-batched because of the existing _CeilingHeight MPB).

VALIDATION P2 (transitions). Capture 2-5 s sequences of each transition at 60 fps and in a forced 30 fps run. Pass when luminance analysis over 341x256 windows finds ≤ 3 general flashes per second (WCAG approximation), including a fixture-flicker scenario; there are no stripe contrast reversals above 3 Hz over more than 25% of the screen; and the dissolve front stays continuous across wall corners and chunk borders (24 m).

VALIDATION P3 (game-state drive). Map events (zone, Relay distance, door opens) to target print states with hysteresis and a minimum dwell, for example 2 s, so a threshold that hovers cannot flicker. Log print-state changes to the autopilot report.json. Pass when the same seed and inputs give an identical print timeline, events reach the screen within 1 frame, and the sound chat's cues line up if any are attached.

PERF GATE (every milestone). Run the autopilot (FrontRoomsMainScenePlaytest, -autopilotSeed 2554 and 20388) plus a scripted Level 0 corridor flythrough, because those seeds start in Office. Run modes: print OFF, P0 static, P1 live but static, P2 animating. Add GPU frame time from FrameTimingManager (always on in the editor) to report.json, because 60 fps is capped. Pass with the spec's absolute gates (average ≥ 55 fps, p99 ≤ 33 ms) and against the baseline (59 fps / p99 ≈ 18 ms in the spec; latest report 58.7 fps, p95 16.8 ms, p99 19.4 ms): average fps −1 or better, p99 +1.5 ms or better, median GPU time +0.5 ms or better at 1080p, and a texture memory delta of +16 MB or less. Repeat once in a macOS Retina player at Ultra quality and once in WebGL, where the browser fps counter has to stand in for GPU timing.

OWNERSHIP: shader, FrontRoomsRenderSetup, gen_surfaces.py and the lookdev capture belong to the visual chat. Removing the _CeilingHeight MPB and the autopilot report fields belong to the map chat (and FrontRooms3DGame). Event hooks are P3 in FrontRooms3DGame and the Hunter; print-change audio belongs to the sound chat. This research changed no files.
open_questions: Art direction: should the paper keep a static embossed relief of the original chevron, so a 'ghost' of the old print shows under raking or flickering light, or should the paper be flat so lighting carries no pattern at all? This decides whether P0b or P0a is the reference look.
Should motion stay inside each 0.75 m roll, registered to the seams like real wallpaper, or flow freely across seams? The second reads more like a projection or an anomaly.

Is the print globally synchronised, per zone, or driven by local events such as a wavefront around the Relay? This decides between a flipbook array with world-space masks and a single shared RenderTexture.

Is WebGL a shipping target or only a demo? It affects the source choice and how much CustomRenderTexture and half-precision testing is needed. CustomRenderTexture support on WebGL2 is not documented, so a test build is needed.
How far are map roots from the origin in real runs? The ring search allows up to 4608 m, and the logs record 'map root'. This decides whether the camera-anchor precision fix is needed now.
Does the edit-mode lookdev preview keep the fixtures steady, with no random flicker? The A/B parity and light-sweep tests depend on it; verify before trusting zero-diff thresholds.
Should the Office, Run and Exit walls get the print too? Drywall and paint have no print; Exit would become a palette row.
Who owns the accessibility 'reduce wall motion' setting and the combined flicker check (visual chat or game/HUD)?

code.title: Shader composite sketch (not applied; for the visual chat): print touches albedo only, sampler reused, global live override with a safe fallback
C# driver sketch (not applied): double-precision phase wrapped on the CPU, globals only

verdicts.claim: In wallpaper(), the ink is baked into height (0.9*blur(ink)), smoothness (+0.07*blur(ink)) and cavity (-0.10*ink), so today's highlights and occlusion follow the chevron.
verdicts.evidence: Tools/lookdev/gen_surfaces.py line 68: height = .18*weave + .9*blur(ink,1.2) + .40*fib + .6*exp(seam); line 70: smooth = .20 + .07*blur(ink,1.0) - .04*mot + .03*(1-fib); line 71: cav = 1 - .35*seam_shadow/.20 - .10*ink. The albedo also carries keep_hue (big - lum)*0.16 and a cream lift, as the report says.

verdicts.claim: In URP 17.3, InitializeBRDFData sets brdfSpecular = lerp(kDielectricSpec, albedo, metallic). With _Metallic = 0 on the wallpapers, specular does not depend on the print.
verdicts.evidence: BRDF.hlsl in the metallic branch (no _SPECULAR_SETUP): brdfSpecular = lerp(kDielectricSpec.rgb, albedo, metallic). L0_Wallpaper.mat, L0_Wallpaper_Shift.mat and Exit_Wallpaper.mat all have _Metallic: 0. Lit.shader:167 declares multi_compile_fragment _ DEBUG_DISPLAY. FrontRoomsSurface.shader has no DEBUG_DISPLAY pragma.

verdicts.claim: The custom DepthNormals pass includes the generic DepthNormalsPass.hlsl, which writes only the vertex normal. No normal map is used, and UVs are used only under _ALPHATEST_ON. SSAO uses depth-normals with a 0.45 m radius.
verdicts.evidence: FrontRoomsSurface.shader:315 includes Shaders/DepthNormalsPass.hlsl. That file declares uv only under _ALPHATEST_ON and outputs NormalizeNormalPerPixel(input.normalWS). FrontRooms_URP_Renderer.asset has SSAO Source: 1 and Radius: 0.45.

verdicts.claim: The project is realtime-only: no baked or realtime lightmaps in all 3 scenes, m_LightProbeSystem 0, and ambient is a fixed Trilight set by FrontRoomsLook.ApplyAmbient. An animated albedo cannot cause a bounce-light mismatch.
verdicts.evidence: FrontRooms3D.unity, FrontRoomsLevelDesigner.unity and FrontRoomsMapTest.unity all have m_EnableBakedLightmaps: 0, m_EnableRealtimeLightmaps: 0 and the built-in LightingDataAsset fileID 20201. FrontRooms_URP.asset has m_LightProbeSystem: 0. FrontRoomsLook.ApplyAmbient sets AmbientMode.Trilight with constant colours. The rendering audit also notes the shader has SH only, with no LIGHTMAP_ON and no APV include. I did not finish the probe grep (a zsh glob error); the absence of LightProbeGroup and ReflectionProbe rests on the report.

verdicts.claim: Precision: the maze never rebases, and the map root can sit 24 x 192 m = 4.6 km out, where planar UVs lose about 1 texel. A CPU camera anchor may be needed.
verdicts.evidence: MapRootFor (FrontRooms3DGame.cs:619-647) loops ring 0..24 with root = (a*192, 0, b*192). But it picks the root so that the map cell under the player's current position (probe - root) is a standard Level 0 row. The map is moved to the player. The player is not moved to the root. So the visible walls are rendered near the player's world position, which stays within about 192 m of the origin because RoomStream.RebaseIfNeeded (stream only, z-axis, and skipped once frozen) keeps it there. A large map-root offset therefore does not put rendered geometry kilometres out. RebaseThreshold = 192 is confirmed, and no rebase exists once the player walks free in the maze. Note also that ring 24 is a Chebyshev ring, so a corner root is 4608*sqrt(2), about 6.5 km.
verdicts.correction: World-space precision depends on how far the player walks from where the stream ended, not on the map root's offset. At a typical start, wall world coordinates are within a few hundred metres of the origin, which is sub-texel. The T5 test at +4608 m tests a case the game does not produce unless the player walks km. The camera-anchor fix is optional. Wrapping the scroll in double on the CPU is still sound.

verdicts.claim: The editor runs Quality High (anisotropicTextures 1 = per texture). Standalone defaults to Ultra (2 = Forced On) and WebGL to High. With Forced On, anisoLevel 1-9 is raised to 9 and 0 disables aniso. On Metal, Vulkan and OpenGL, mip and aniso filtering are independent.
verdicts.evidence: QualitySettings.asset: m_CurrentQuality: 3 (High, anisotropicTextures: 1); Ultra has anisotropicTextures: 2; m_PerPlatformDefaultQuality Standalone: 5, WebGL: 3. The Unity Texture.anisoLevel doc quotes the 1-9 to 9 rule, the 0 opt-out and the Metal/Vulkan/OpenGL independence. The surface importer sets Trilinear, anisoLevel 16 and Repeat (FrontRoomsRenderSetup.cs:625-627). Caveat: the report says a RenderTexture 'left at its default aniso level' gets forced aniso in the Mac build. That depends on RenderTexture's default anisoLevel being 1 or more, which I did not verify. If it is 0, Forced On does not apply.

verdicts.claim: The cameras use AntialiasingMode.None plus 4x MSAA. URP docs say MSAA does not fix texture or shader aliasing, and that TAA cannot be used with MSAA.
verdicts.evidence: FrontRoomsPostStack.cs:72 sets data.antialiasing = AntialiasingMode.None. FrontRooms_URP.asset has m_MSAA: 4. The URP anti-aliasing page says MSAA 'does not fix shader aliasing issues such as specular or texture aliasing' and 'you can't use MSAA with TAA'. The claim that TAA would ghost a texture-space animation is the report's own inference and was not verified.

verdicts.claim: SRP Batcher: GameObjects must not use MaterialPropertyBlocks, and material properties must live in one UnityPerMaterial CBUFFER. FrontRoomsMapWorld.AddRenderer gives every shell renderer whose material has _CeilingHeight an MPB, so map shells are already not batched.
verdicts.evidence: The SRPBatcher-Materials page says 'The GameObject mustn't use MaterialPropertyBlocks' and requires all material properties in a single UnityPerMaterial CBUFFER. FrontRoomsMapWorld.cs:745-768 builds a MaterialPropertyBlock with _CeilingHeight and calls r.SetPropertyBlock whenever material.HasProperty(CeilingHeightId). The shader declares the CBUFFER in HLSLINCLUDE (lines 52-71).

verdicts.claim: Sampler reuse: inline samplers work only on D3D11/12 and Metal, separate samplers are not available on OpenGL ES, and D3D11 allows 128 textures but only 16 samplers.
verdicts.evidence: The current 6000.3 SL-SamplerStates page says 'Inline samplers don't work if you target the OpenGL ES or OpenGL Core graphics APIs', so Vulkan is not excluded. It describes the fallback to a combined sampler2D on APIs without separate samplers, and confirms sampler reuse through the _NOSAMPLER and _SAMPLER macros. My fetch did not surface the 128/16 figures.
verdicts.correction: Inline samplers are excluded on GLES and GLCore. The page does not say they work only on D3D11/12 and Metal. The practical advice still holds: reusing sampler_BaseMap on Metal, and on WebGL2 the texture's own sampler settings apply.

verdicts.claim: _Time is a float4 (t/20, t, 2t, 3t), and Time.timeAsDouble gives more precision over long periods.
verdicts.evidence: The built-in shader variables doc gives _Time = (t/20, t, t*2, t*3). The timeAsDouble doc says it 'offers more precision than a float or single value, particularly over extended periods of real-world time'.

verdicts.claim: Film grain is re-seeded every frame by Random.InitState(Time.frameCount). Project post values: grain Medium3 0.22, CA 0.06 (Office 0.03), bloom threshold 1.05 and intensity 0.55, lens distortion -0.04.
verdicts.evidence: PostProcessUtils.cs (~line 103) calls Random.InitState(Time.frameCount). FrontRoomsRenderSetup.cs (lines 180-240) overrides grain Medium3 0.22, CA 0.06 and 0.03, bloom 1.05/0.55, lens -0.04.

verdicts.claim: Print-source platform facts: texture arrays are supported on WebGL 2.0, VideoClips aren't supported on Web (URL only, no frame accuracy), and FrameTimingManager GPU time is unsupported on WebGL but supported on macOS Metal.
verdicts.evidence: The texture-arrays page lists 'OpenGL ES 3.0 (Android, WebGL 2.0)'. The webgl-video page says 'VideoClips aren't supported on Web', 'Use the Video Player component's URL option' and 'Web doesn't support frame accuracy'. The frame-timing-manager page marks WebGL as partial ('GPU Frame Time measurement is unsupported') and macOS Metal as supported. The fetch did not confirm that FrameTimingManager is 'always active in the editor and development builds'.

verdicts.claim: WCAG 2.2 sets at most 3 general or red flashes per second, an area limit of 25% of any 10° field, and a 341x256 px approximation.

gaps: The biggest error is in the precision section. MapRootFor moves the map under the player, not the player out to the map root. Rendered walls stay near the stream's rebased world origin. The real risk is the distance the player walks in the maze after the stream freezes. The T5 offsets (+1536 and +4608 m) and the camera-anchor fix should be reframed as a distance-walked test. They are not inherent to the map-root offset.
The Chebyshev ring search means the maximum root offset is about 6.5 km on the diagonal, not 4.6 km. This is moot given the point above.

The report's claim that a RenderTexture at its default aniso level would get forced aniso at Ultra depends on RenderTexture.anisoLevel's default, which neither the report nor I checked. A default of 0 would opt out of Forced On. Setting anisoLevel explicitly (as recommended) removes the issue.

The editor quality level depends on what the Quality window selects in the editor (m_CurrentQuality 3). Play mode does not automatically use the Standalone default. The report states this correctly, but the autopilot baseline caveat should mention that tests can call QualitySettings.SetQualityLevel(5) to match the build.

Environment specular (unity_SpecCube0 / GlossyEnvironmentReflection) is not discussed. For metallic 0 it is scaled by the albedo-independent brdfSpecular, so the conclusion holds. But RenderSettings.reflectionIntensity is set by FrontRoomsLook and the sky cubemap's content was not inspected.
The report does not check whether FrontRoomsSurface.shader's ForwardLit hard-codes metallic or reads _Metallic. The .mat files are 0, but the shader path was not traced.
The ITC/Ofcom stripe-pattern rule is quoted second-hand (the PDF returned 403). Treat it as unverified until it is checked against the published Ofcom guidance.
The GPU cost (0.05-0.3 ms) and the RenderTexture bandwidth figures are untested arithmetic estimates. The Wikipedia URL is given as en.wikipedia.com, a typo for en.wikipedia.org.
The project-wide grep for LightProbeGroup and ReflectionProbe in scenes and prefabs was not independently re-run here because of a shell glob error. That absence rests on the report's own check.
